body:
Issue is operational (coordinating the first crush/drop tests on Jeff Hill's tower) and this repo is the LaTeX MRG proposal with no code or existing test-protocol surface. This PR consolidates the moving parts from the issue thread, adds a literature synthesis, and analyzes the recorded accelerometer data.

### Added
- **`docs/drop-test-protocol.md`** — single source of truth for the drop-test setup, covering:
  - Equipment + links to the TP4 Quick Start / User's Guide PDFs attached on the issue and the training video (https://youtu.be/RNjpAmWWmkQ)
  - The tower is **bungee-assisted** (base accelerates past 1 g): §3.1 reframes the pre-impact specimen lift-off as intrinsic rig physics rather than a setup artifact, and §5 leads with Jeff's first-pass fix (cap how far the specimen's top can rise relative to the base) plus tie-to-base options
  - Quantities of interest tied to the BO objective stack: `g_max`, SEA, full ~10 s ringdown (not just the 200 ms shock), reusability, slow-mo framing from t=0
  - Failure modes from the first instrumented drop: bungee-driven specimen lift-off pre-impact, ~25° cage tilt from loose rod/hole clearance, slow-mo starting after hoist release
  - @sgbaird's three-test next-iteration plan: bare specimen → plate-only (uninstrumented) → instrumented cage drop
  - Mitigations: constrain specimen to base / cap upward travel, tighter rod/plate tolerance (re-drill or thin metal plates, optionally linear bushings), top-plate retention clips, longer-term vertex-mounted accelerometer inside an acrylic cage, independent lab access for all three students
  - Cross-references to companion modalities out of scope for the first drop (high-speed camera, shaker transfer function, slug-firing gas gun, Polytec LDV)

- **`edison-trajectories/drop-test/`** — Edison Scientific LITERATURE_HIGH synthesis (task `653d7d39`) on drop-tower troubleshooting for small 3D-printed lattice/tensegrity specimens: ~57 KB report, full JSON dump, submission record, and README. Idempotent driver at **`scripts/edison/submit_drop_test.py`**. Surfaces a standards stack (ASTM D5276/D7136/D3332, ISO 6603/1683/5347, MIL-STD-810 method 516, SAE J211) and recommendations (linear sleeve bearings, magnetic/elastic top-plate hold-down, ≥10 s ring-buffer DAQ, SAE J211 CFC filtering, n ≥ 5 + CV, ≥5000 fps DIC; closest analogues Pajunen 2019, Dwyer 2023).

- **First drop-test data analysis** of the five TP4 accelerometer exports posted by @me-madsen (`Signal 10–14`, 4-channel, 125 kHz, 0.2 s window):
  - **`data/drop-tests/raw/`** — committed raw export files
  - **`scripts/analysis/drop_test_analysis.py`** — loader, SAE J211 CFC-1000 / CFC-180 filtering, peak/pulse/PSD metrics, and figure generation
  - **`data/drop-tests/figures/`** — full-window CH1 overlay, per-run impact zoom (raw vs filtered), peak-g bar chart, PSD, and CH4 trigger-artifact plot
  - **`docs/drop-test-analysis.md`** + **`data/drop-tests/README.md`** — findings: the "audrey" tensegrity specimen reduces CFC-180 peak acceleration ~74–79 % vs the no-specimen control (~370–463 G vs ~1,792 G), while the PETG run's raw peak is within ~1 % of the control (≈ direct plate-on-plate hit), strong evidence of the bungee-driven lift-off; CH4 carries a fixed ~1.4 kG trigger/release artifact at t≈4.2 ms in every run. Caveats noted: unconfirmed channel map, 200 ms window only, n = 1 for control/PETG, no Δv/SEA quoted yet.

- **Vertex vs. acrylic-plate T3-prism drop-test data and analysis** posted by @ctrhjk (PR #67), under **`data/drop-tests/vertex-acrylic/`**:
  - **`raw/`** — eight TP4 exports `{n0jdwk, m6cyoq, T3_0103, T3_0000}_Signal{1,2}.csv` (`Signal1` = vertex-mounted, `Signal2` = acrylic-plate), single drop per configuration at 13 ft, 200 ms / 125 kHz
  - **`README.md`** — channel map (CH1 removed; CH2–CH4 tri-axis; CH5 single-axis; CH4 = 1000 G trigger) with full-scale/sensitivity per channel, per-specimen file index, and @ctrhjk's observations (clip-height/no-trigger issue, hot-glue z-axis mount limitation, `m6cyoq` strut and `T3_0103` TPU-tendon damage after the acrylic test, and the invalid `T3_0000` acrylic run where the accelerometer fell off)
  - **`scripts/analysis/drop_test_vertex_acrylic_analysis.py`** — locates the impact via the triggered CH4 channel (windowed ±1.5 ms peak search in the first 10 ms, not a global max), baseline-corrects, and reports raw / SAE J211 CFC-1000 / CFC-180 peaks for the single-axis CH5 (primary go-forward sensor) and tri-axis CH4, auto-flagging invalid / no-clean-impact runs
  - **`data/drop-tests/vertex-acrylic/figures/`** — vertex-vs-acrylic CH5 impact windows, CFC-180 peak-g bar chart, and vertex CH5 PSD
  - **`docs/drop-test-vertex-acrylic-analysis.md`** — findings + an explicit **SOP / test-method** section: vertex mounting is repeatable (4/4 clean, CFC-180 229–284 G, CV ≈ 9 %) while the acrylic configuration is not (3/4 runs registered no clean impact — clips too low so the plate seats on the specimen, plus the fell-off `T3_0000`); the vertex peaks do not yet discriminate geometry so fresh intact distinct-geometry samples (vertex-only, n ≥ 5) are needed before peak-g is a trustworthy BO objective; replace the hot-glue mount with a z-axis-aligned seat; and the single-axis sensor's raw peaks reach 70–90 % of its 9,442.9 G full scale (near saturation on the m6cyoq-acrylic run). Caveats: n = 1 per (specimen, mount), 200 ms window only, partial-pulse Δv, unconfirmed CH4/CH5 axis correspondence.

- **Clip-height sweep & base-plate accelerometer-check diagnostic** posted by @ctrhjk, under **`data/drop-tests/clip-height/`** — drilling into why the acrylic-plate configuration repeatedly fails to trigger:
  - **`raw/Accelerometer_check_Signal1.csv`** + **`README.md`** — the one triggered base-plate CSV (tri-axis on the bottom plate, 13 in drop) plus a setup README documenting both experiments: the clip-height sweep (extra bungees cured fly-off; tri-axis on the acrylic plate; clips at 0.5/1/1.5/2 in, two drops each; **0/8 drops triggered**, video only) and the base-plate accelerometer check, with the shared channel map
  - **`scripts/analysis/drop_test_clip_height_analysis.py`** + **`data/drop-tests/clip-height/figures/`** — windowed CH4 impact location, SAE J211 CFC-1000 / CFC-180 peak/pulse/Δv metrics, and figures (base-plate impact window, full-window CH4, PSD)
  - **`docs/drop-test-clip-height-analysis.md`** — findings: the base-plate hit triggers cleanly (CH4 raw 3072 G ≈ 3.1× the 1000 G trigger, CFC-180 280 G, Δv ≈ 3.3 m/s; CH4 dominates the off-axis channels ~23–55×), so the acrylic-plate "no trigger" failure (0/8 across the clip sweep) is a **load-path** problem — the plate seats on / is damped by the bungee-restrained specimen — not the sensor, DAQ, or trigger level.

- **Input-output (transmissibility) drop-test data and analysis** posted by @ctrhjk (PR #67), under **`data/drop-tests/input-output/`** — @ctrhjk's input-output instrumentation design: a single-axis accelerometer on the bottom plate = **input** (now the triggered channel CH5), a tri-axis accelerometer hot-glued to the top vertex = **output** (CH2–CH4), **bungees removed**, four distinct-geometry specimens (`practice`, `n0jdwk`, `yqpmx1`, `h8Lbev`) each dropped five times at 13 in:
  - **`raw/`** — 20 TP4 exports `{practice,n0jdwk,yqpmx1,h8Lbev}_Signal{1..5}.csv` (`Signal` index = drop number) + **`README.md`** with the channel map (trigger moved to the single-axis input CH5) and @ctrhjk's setup notes
  - **`scripts/analysis/drop_test_input_output_analysis.py`** — locates the impact on the triggered CH5 (windowed ±1.5 ms peak), baseline-corrects, and reports raw / SAE J211 CFC-1000 / CFC-180 peaks for the input (CH5) and the tri-axis output resultant, the transmissibility `T = output/input`, pulse width and Δv, with per-specimen mean ± 1σ / CV aggregates
  - **`data/drop-tests/input-output/figures/`** — input-vs-output impact windows (5 drops overlaid), transmissibility bar chart, input repeatability, output PSD
  - **`docs/drop-test-input-output-analysis.md`** — findings: the input-output design works — **20/20 drops triggered cleanly**, removing the bungees makes the input nearly constant (235–248 G CFC-180, ≤1.7 % CV), and **transmissibility now discriminates geometry** (`yqpmx1` ≈ 0.96 is the only attenuator, `h8Lbev` ≈ 1.09, `practice`/`n0jdwk` ≈ 1.17–1.19), making `T` (or output-peak-at-fixed-input) a usable BO objective; a mild within-run drift across the five cyclic drops is flagged as most likely hot-glue-mount-driven. Caveats: n = 1 specimen per geometry (5 repeat drops), 200 ms window, unverified tri-axis orientation, IDs not yet tied back to design parameters
  - **`edison-trajectories/input-output/`** — Edison Scientific ANALYSIS (task `fe044079`) that independently **reproduced the transmissibility values exactly to two decimals**, confirmed the within-run drift is statistically real and mount-driven (pooled +0.015/drop, p = 0.0001), endorsed `T` as a first-pass screening objective (recommending FRF / SRS-band metrics and output-peak-at-fixed-input as it matures), and gave a prioritized SOP (rigid z-aligned keyed sensor seat, keep bungees removed, extend capture past 200 ms, n ≥ 5 distinct prints per geometry with randomized order, anchor in SAE J211 / ISO 5347 / ASTM D3332). Idempotent driver **`scripts/edison/submit_input_output.py`** + fetch **`scripts/edison/fetch_input_output.py`**; a cross-check section is folded into the analysis doc.
title: Add drop-test protocol, Edison synthesis, and first-data analysis

body: Audrey's manual paint protocol (bottom-view stripes along each member's centerline, ~1/3 projected width, trimmed at vertex overlaps except the three bed-contact vertices which are connected triangularly) is laborious, gets wiped whenever the source mesh is re-rendered, and does not generalize across the structure families and parameter sweeps planned in PR #22. This PR replaces the paint step with a **general-purpose, single-material PLA support recipe for Bambu Studio** that works on any tensegrity topology without per-geometry tuning, **plus a manually-baked narrowing-pillar / tree-support STL workflow for any print that contains vertical or near-vertical members (e.g. the vertical TPU cables of a T-prism)**. Overhang analysis can never flag a perfectly vertical cylinder as an overhang regardless of `support_threshold_angle` value — it has no down-facing surface — so the slicer settings alone are physically incapable of placing supports under vertical cables. The narrowing-pillar path was therefore promoted to the recommended TPU-safe path (replacing the Support Enforcer STL approach, which still proved unreliable in practice and is kept only as a secondary fallback). The headless verification toolchain now targets the actual **Bambu Lab H2D 0.4 nozzle** system profile via the **genuine Bambu Studio CLI** (the `bambu-studio` binary shipped in the BambuStudio Linux AppImage). The previously-used OrcaSlicer fork has been dropped: the Ubuntu 24.04 Bambu Studio build links libsoup-3.0 / WebKit2GTK-4.1 (the older 2.4 / 4.0 dependency was only an issue on legacy AppImage builds) and runs cleanly under xvfb, so we no longer need a community fork to drive the same `resources/profiles/BBL/` bundle. The PyPI `bambu-cli` package is a printer-control MQTT client, not a slicer, so it isn't applicable here. ### Changes #### Path (a) — Bambu Studio settings recipe (no painting, no per-geometry code) Suitable on its own for **PLA-only** prints whose members all have a meaningful tilt away from vertical. - **`cad/print-supports/README.md`** — derives the override set that reproduces Audrey's "centerline stripes, ~1/3 member width, no vertex overlaps, three bed-vertices bridged" pattern from the slicer's overhang analysis instead of paint flags: - `support_type = tree(auto)` + `support_on_build_plate_only = 1` (branches root at the plate, never on a member — matches the bottom-view-only rule). - `support_threshold_angle = 10` (flags the entire down-facing side of every tilted member as an overhang so the tree generator builds branches from the plate all the way along each strut's bottom). Documented limitation: this still cannot cover perfectly vertical surfaces (there's no down-facing geometry to detect); use §C for those. - `tree_support_tip_diameter = 0.8` + `tree_support_branch_distance = 2.5` (reproduces the ~1/3-of-member-width stripe coverage). - `bridge_no_support = 1` (the three bottom-triangle cables bridge cleanly between bed-contact vertices). - `brim_type = outer_only`, `brim_width = 5` (insurance against tip-over for the tiny node footprints). - **`cad/print-supports/bambu-pla-tensegrity-process.json`** — one-shot importable process-override snippet (`Process → Add → Import process`). #### Path (c) — manually-baked narrowing-pillar / tree-support STL generator (**primary TPU-safe path / any structure with vertical members**) Tapered contact pillars are baked directly into the printable mesh — bottom view, narrowing upward from the bed to a small contact patch on the underside of each member. Because they are part of the printed object (not slicer supports), they print reliably regardless of slicer behaviour around vertical cylinders, are visible in any STL viewer before sending to the printer, and snap off cleanly after printing. The generator now defaults to a **Bambu-Studio-style `--tree` mode** (in response to print-floor feedback that the earlier one-cone-per-cell pillars were effectively solid columns that fused onto the part and tore it on removal, and built up too much material on the plate): - **`--tree` mode** — slim Ø~0.4 mm breakaway contact tips merge pairwise into thin, near-hollow Ø~1.8 mm self-supporting branches (kept within `--max_branch_angle`, default 40°, of vertical) that converge agglomeratively onto just a **few trunk feet** on the build plate instead of one wide base per pillar. This dramatically reduces both the part-contact area (clean snap-off, no fused infill) and the build-plate footprint. Branch/trunk/tip diameters are tunable via `--branch_d`, `--trunk_d`, `--tip_d`; merging is controlled by `--merge_radius`. All emitted geometry is clamped to the build plate (`z ≥ base_z`). - **Contact-tip diameter benchmarked against Bambu Studio** — in response to review feedback that the connection points looked wide, the tip diameter was checked against Bambu's own numbers (`tree_support_tip_diameter` defaults to **0.8 mm**, with official guidance to shrink it toward **0.3–0.4 mm for fine/delicate features**). The previous Ø 0.6 mm tip flared to the branch over only 1.5 mm, giving a ~0.8 mm effective contact footprint at the part (right at Bambu's default). The defaults are now **`--tip_d 0.4` mm** (one nozzle width — finer than Bambu's default, matching its delicate-feature guidance; the tip is buried `--tip_overshoot 0.3` mm into the member so it still slices reliably) and **`--tip_contact_h 2.5` mm** (up from 1.5 mm) so the slim neck stays narrow for longer before flaring to branch width, dropping the surface contact footprint from ~0.8 mm to ~0.55 mm. Both knobs remain CLI-tunable. - **`cad/print-supports/generate_support_pillars.py`** — geometry-agnostic generator. Three placement modes, each usable with or without `--tree`: - **`--stl part.stl` (mesh-ray-cast mode, primary)** — uses `trimesh`'s ray-intersection engine to look "up from the build plate" through the actual printable mesh. For each cell of an XY grid (`--spacing`, default 4 mm for the committed artefacts) it casts a +Z ray and inspects **every** triangle the ray crosses (`multiple_hits=True`), classifying each by its face normal: a closed solid is entered through a *down-facing* face (a member's underside) and exited through an *up-facing* one. A contact tip is placed under **each** down-facing underside that sits above `--min_clearance` and has more than `--min_gap` mm of open air directly below it (so faces already resting on the plate or on a lower member are skipped); the `--down_normal_max` knob sets how steep a face still counts as down-facing. In tree mode those undersides become the branch tips. This replaced an earlier `multiple_hits=False` version that recorded only the single *lowest* surface per XY column — which silently dropped every member stacked above another one, most importantly the bottom end-caps of the vertical TPU cables that hang above the struts, so they printed unsupported and the print failed. Walking all crossings now guarantees a tip on the underside of every member at every height — including joint-sphere bulges, fillets, members crossing over other members, and any other geometry the centerline-sampling / lowest-hit modes missed. The committed run (`--spacing 4 --min_clearance 1.5 --min_gap 1.0 --merge_radius 22`) yields **188** tips spanning z ≈ 1.6–126.1 mm (verified by `verify_support_geometry.py` to land on the part underside to within 0.0000 mm, with all feet clamped to the plate). - **`--topology t3_prism|prism_n`** preset (built-in, no extra dep) — parametric centerline sampling along each member. - **`--members my_members.json`** (list of `{p1, p2, d, trim_ends}`) — parametric centerline sampling for arbitrary structures. - Pure-Python binary-STL writer; `numpy` always; `trimesh` only for the `--stl` ray-cast mode. #### Path (c′, fallback) — geometry-agnostic Support Enforcer STL generator Kept as a secondary fallback for users who want to drive supports through the slicer rather than baking them into the mesh. - **`cad/print-supports/generate_support_enforcers.py`** — geometry-agnostic enforcer-STL generator. Same `--members JSON` / `--topology preset` interface; vertical members emit footprint enforcers via `--vertical_pad`. #### Support verification — geometry checks + layer-by-layer CalculiX FEA (`cad/print-supports/verification/`) Added in response to a print failure where the committed support STL was found to be **stale** — re-casting the underside rays against the real PR #35 mesh produces **188** contact points (z ≈ 1.6–126.1 mm), but the previously committed `t3-prism-pr35-pillars.stl` held only 181 (topping out at z ≈ 112 mm), so the **7 top-cap / joint undersides were missing** and the highest members printed unsupported. The artefacts are regenerated and two automated, reproducible verification tools now gate against this recurring (eyeballing the preview was not enough): - **`verify_support_geometry.py`** (new) — uses trimesh's exact ray/proximity engine, exits non-zero on any failure. Four invariants, all **PASS** on the committed artefact: - **CONTACT** — every tip lands on the part underside (max gap **0.0000 mm**). - **REALISED** — every intended tip is present in the committed STL (the check that caught the stale artefact; max tip→pillar **0.30 mm** = the `--tip_overshoot`). - **ON-PLATE** — no geometry below z = 0; **662** foot vertices on the build plate. - **COVERAGE** — re-samples undersides at 2× density: **99.3 %** of flat overhangs (face normal nz < −0.7; near-vertical walls self-support) within 5 mm of a support, worst **6.3 mm** (within PLA's bridge), 0 beyond 8 mm. - **`fea_support_stability.py`** (new) — CalculiX (`ccx`) layer-by-layer FEA. Reconstructs the emitted branch network, extracts the worst-case column (longest continuous run = **108.5 mm**, 1.2° from vertical, Ø1.8–3.1 mm) and grows it from the plate: self-weight **buckling** min safety factor **61×** (PASS), **tip-over** COM margin **27.8 mm** inside the convex hull of 1148 plate contacts / 79 mm base span (PASS), plus a documented worst-case **lateral-compliance** caveat (a fully free-standing 108 mm Ø1.8 mm column is floppy, but never stands free in practice — neighbouring struts/branches print in lockstep, in-print forces are ~hundredths of a N, the 5 mm brim anchors the feet; bump `--trunk_d` or `--merge_radius` to brace a taller lone column). Produces `t3-prism-pr35-fea-stability.png`. - **`render_pillars_preview.py`** (new) — still iso + bottom-view preview renderer (the preview PNG previously had no committed generator), matching the rotating-GIF scene/colours. - The geometry + FEA checks answer the two questions that actually failed the print ("does every support touch the part?" / "will the supports stand up?") more rigorously than a sliced preview. As a final on-hardware-profile confirmation, the combined printable mesh is **also driven through the live `bambu-studio` CLI** — see the slice subsection below. #### End-to-end verification on PR #35 T3-prism (`cad/print-supports/verification/`) — Bambu Lab H2D + Bambu Studio CLI - **`slice_bambu_h2d.py`** (renamed from `slice_h2d.py`) — headless slicing driver. Resolves the BambuStudio AppImage's bundled **Bambu Lab H2D 0.4 nozzle** machine profile, walks the `inherits` chain through the matching process + `Bambu PLA Basic @BBL H2D` filament, layers the tensegrity overrides from `bambu-pla-tensegrity-process.json` on top, and invokes the `bambu-studio` CLI under xvfb. Supports the path-(a) auto-only flow, the path-(c) baked-pillar flow (slice the combined mesh with `--no-repo-overrides --override enable_support=0`, keeping the 5 mm brim), and the path-(c′) enforcer flow. - **On-hardware-profile slice of the baked-pillar mesh (path (c))** — the actual printable mesh `t3-prism-pr35-with-pillars.stl` (part + baked tree pillars) slices end-to-end with no errors on the genuine BambuStudio 02.06.00.51 CLI / Bambu Lab H2D 0.4 nozzle PLA profile: **646 layers, max_z 129.20 mm, 20 094 mm / 60.90 g filament, ~5 h 36 m**. Because the pillars are baked into the mesh, slicer-side support generation is disabled so it slices as one solid object. (Running the Ubuntu-24.04 AppImage CLI headlessly requires the `libgstreamer1.0-0`, `libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-0`, `libsoup-3.0-0`, `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0`, `libgtk-3-0` apt libs.) - **`render_gcode.py`** — gained a **`--baked-supports`** mode so the gcode preview is honest for a single-object (baked-pillar) slice: the slicer emits no `Support` features, so the panels are relabelled to show the object (members + baked pillars) coloured by layer height plus the pillar feet + brim that land on the plate. The default (path-(a) slicer-supports) behaviour is unchanged. - **`diff_supports.py`**, **`gcode_to_stl.py`**, **`merge_stls.py`** — gcode parsers/renderers and STL utilities, unchanged from prior revisions of this PR. - **`render_pillars_gif.py`** — small matplotlib-based renderer that loads the combined part+pillars STL and writes a rotating 360° GIF (configurable frame count, elevation, FPS, resolution) so the bed-up support coverage can be verified visually from every angle without an external viewer. - **`build_enforcer_3mf.py`** — bundles a printable STL + an enforcer STL into a single 3MF with the enforcer marked `volume_type=SupportEnforcer` (used only for the fallback enforcer path). - **`t3-prism-pr35-pillars.stl`** (regenerated, tree mode with the finer Ø 0.4 mm contact tips and the multi-hit underside ray-cast, **188 contact tips / 31 trunk feet / 23,520 tris**) — tree-support mesh produced by `generate_support_pillars.py --stl … --tree` ray-cast against the actual PR #35 T3-prism printable mesh, so every down-facing underside the bed's-eye rays cross gets a tip (including the vertical-cable end-caps, members stacked above struts, and the top-cap / joint undersides the prior stale 181-tip pass missed) while branching off only a handful of feet on the plate. - **`t3-prism-pr35-with-pillars.stl`** (regenerated, **50,336 tris**) — combined printable STL (T3-prism + ray-cast tree supports merged via `merge_stls.py`), ready to slice as a single solid object with no slicer-side support material required. - **`t3-prism-pr35-pillars-preview.png`** (regenerated, via `render_pillars_preview.py`) — iso + bottom-view render showing the T3-prism part in grey with the ray-cast tree supports (orange) branching from a few feet up to the underside of each member at every height, including the joint-sphere bulges and the vertical-cable end-caps the prior lowest-hit pass missed. - **`t3-prism-pr35-pillars-gcode-preview.png`** (new, via `render_gcode.py --baked-supports`) — 3-panel render of the on-hardware-profile slice of the combined part+pillars mesh: bottom view + first-layer panels show every baked pillar foot and member base landing on the bed inside the brim, and the height-coloured iso panel confirms the toolpath spans the full z ≈ 0–126 mm with everything rooted on the plate. - **`t3-prism-pr35-pillars-rotating.gif`** (regenerated) — rotating 360° turntable animation of the combined part+pillars mesh (object grey, supports orange), produced by `render_pillars_gif.py`, for full-angle visual verification of support-to-underside coverage. - body:
Print-in-place tensegrity specimens (PR #35) deposit TPU tendons at a mix of 0°/45°/90° relative to the bead direction, which biases strength-dominated tests more than stiffness-dominated ones. This PR adds an analysis answering how much that affects the experiments planned across the open PRs.

### Deliverable
- New `reviews/tendon_print_angle_impact.md` (style matches `reviews/mock_reviews.md` and `literature/davami2025-analysis.md`).

### Contents
- **Mechanism** — why the geometry *guarantees* a 0°/45°/90° tendon population for any single build orientation; why slender tendons + TPU 85A + captive-core joints sharpen the effect vs. typical FFF coupons.
- **Anisotropy bracket** (FFF-TPU literature, not yet measured on our parts): σ_90°/σ_0° ≈ 0.3–0.6; E_90°/E_0° ≈ 0.7–0.9. Strength is the dominant concern; stiffness is mostly preserved.
- **FoM-class effect** — small for stiffness-like FoMs (initial Instron slope, low-f transfer function, F_pre), large for first-failure FoMs, medium and load-path-dependent for SEA / h_crit / peak-g.
- **Per-PR severity table** (L/M/H) with mitigations for #28, #33, #35, #39/#52, #45, #47, #49/#50, #54, #56, #58, #60. Highlights:
  - **H** — PR #35 (build orientation is currently frozen in the Sobol batch generator) and generalization beyond PR #52's fixed-orientation DOE.
  - **M** — sim↔experiment validation in #33, egg-drop h_crit in #47, the FFF-vs-SLA delta in #58 (Davami used isotropic Tough 2000), and the cross-modality objective synthesis in #60.
  - **L** — equipment/doc PRs (#28, #45, #56) and the initial sub-densification Instron run (#50).
- **Five ranked mitigations**, cheapest first:
  1. Per-tendon angle dump from the sliced gcode (extend PR #35's `patch_mm_extruder.py`).
  2. Sobol replicates at ≥2 build orientations.
  3. `k_anisotropy(theta)` scalar in `simulations/printable_design.py`.
  4. Promote `build_orientation` from frozen context to a categorical Ax design parameter (PRs #30/#35/#60).
  5. Structural fix: post-print manual TPU threading via PR #52's noted alternative path — fully decouples tendon strength from slicer-decided angles.
- **Near-term follow-ups** assigned per PR (#35 gcode log + unfreeze orientation; #50 add "first-tendon-to-fail + angle bin" to the Instron metadata schema; #52 add a 3-cell × {0°,45°,90°} sanity sub-array; #33/#60 plumb a single `anisotropy_ratio` knob).
- **Scope guard** — explicitly notes what is *not* invalidated: PR #35 captive-core joint, PR #45 strut-material recommendation, PR #50 protocol, PR #28 LDV resolution.

body: From our latest print https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/pull/35#issuecomment-4502140147 we noticed that the tendons of the tensegrity structure are noticeably printed at different angles. We expect that this will lead to certain cables tending to fail more consistently. It's likely that the tendons that print parallel to their direction will be strongest. It may be worth measuring which cables fail first during tests and exploring ways to minimize inconsistencies during printing cables. It is expected that this problem cannot be entirely avoided while printing a tensegrity specimen as one "pre-assembled" piece due to varying tendon angles. It may be possible to optimize which tendons are printed at what angles (i.e. what orientation the structure is printed in) so that the tendons that are likely to take more force will be printed at more ideal angles. A tendon that printed parallel to the tendon direction. A tendon that printed at about a 45 degree angle relative to the tendon direction. A tendon that printed roughly perpendicular to the tendon direction.

body:
Companion synthesis for the issue asking how strut curvature could shape the project beyond width/slenderness sweeps, including the explicit creative idea of paired struts buckling together into a bistable, locked mode. Modeled on `edison-trajectories/tpu-petg-bo-variables-additions-from-pr22.md` (PR #24).

### Changes

- **New file:** `edison-trajectories/strut-curvature-explorations.md`
- **§1 Why curvature ≠ width.** Imperfection-seeded buckling sets *direction* of collapse independent of `P_cr`; turning print-induced bow into a deterministic axis converts noise into a control knob (programmed snap, lower repeatable peak F, geometric pre-stress that offsets the small TPU 85A prestress budget).
- **§2 Seven new BO axes** to slot alongside the 5ae24eaf table and PR #24 §A/§B:

  | Axis | Domain | Conditional on |
  |---|---|---|
  | `strut_shape` | {straight, single_arc, S_arc, helical, tapered_arc} | — |
  | `curvature_amplitude δ/L` | `[0, 0.05]` | shape ≠ straight |
  | `curvature_plane φ` | `[0°, 90°]` | arc shapes |
  | `helix_pitch_ratio p/L` | `[0.5, 4]` | helical |
  | `taper_ratio` | `[0.6, 1.0]` | tapered/helical |
  | `pair_coordination` | {independent, parallel_sign, antiparallel_sign, chiral_pair} | N_struts ≥ 2 |
  | `snap_through_target` (constraint) | `[0.05, 0.5]·P_cr` | bistable_mode ≠ monostable |

- **§3 Coordinated-pair bistable mode** — the issue's creative ask. Two parallel-sign curved struts latch via a printed TPU 85A bump-and-pocket at mid-span: hysteretic EA (~halved rebound vs monostable), `2^N_bay` passive shape space across stacked Snelson bays, lateral squeeze re-arms.
- **§4 Manufacturability on H2D.** `δ/L ≤ 5%` stays inside the 3-perimeter envelope at strut Ø ≥ 2 mm; helical printable in-place down to `p/L ≈ 0.5`. Joint coupling to issue #38 is a one-line bore rotation `α = atan(2δ/L)` in `B_dovetail.scad` / `A_anchor_bulb.scad` — no new joint family.
- **§5 Failure modes.** Curvature shifts dominant mode toward hinge-yield — log per-specimen so the surrogate learns the flip. Bistable pairs add cyclic-fatigue risk on `N_reuse`; latched state is class-2, gate behind joint-design Phase-4.
- **§6 Next actions.** `strut_shape` arg in `simulations/printable_design.py` + re-run `simulations/newton_drop.py`; Edison LITERATURE_HIGH on coordinated-pair bistable buckling (Restrepo 2015, Frenzel 2016, Pan 2023, Schenk & Guest); conservative initial enable-set (curvature on, paired bistability gated).

No code, dependency, or CI changes.

body: Pre-tensioning the anchor-bulb requires a PLA↔TPU bore bond weak enough to pull through under finite force, **and** an air gap small enough that the TPU still prints as a clean cylinder when bridging the bore horizontally against gravity. This adds a single H2D plate that sweeps **air gap × joint size** for the **A3 countersunk** anchor head so we can pull-test each cell and pick a winner in one print job. ### `cad/anchor-bulb-tensioning-array/` - **`_common.scad`** — A3 countersunk joint (90° conical TPU head mating a 90° countersink cut into the +Y face of the PLA node, flush + self-centring + ~8.8 mm² conical bearing wall) + 16×26×4 mm pull-test tab, parameterized on `(node_d, gap_r)`. Per-material modules (`*_pla` / `*_tpu`) and a colour-preserving X=0 section module. - **15 specimen files** — `H-S{0,1,2}G{0..4}.scad`, one per DOE cell with embossed ID on the tab: - **Joint size** (rows): node Ø **7.5 / 9.5 / 12.0 mm** (S0 / S1 / S2). S1 = PR #39 Phase-3 default; S2 = matches dovetail node OD; S0 = smallest with ≥2 PLA wall perimeters at the equator. Bore length tracks node Ø, so this axis tests whether a longer horizontal bridge tolerates a different gap. - **Air gap** (columns): radial clearance **0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.6 mm** (G0 … G4); bore Ø = 2.4 mm cable + 2·gap. - **`tensioning_array.scad`** — 3×5 grid, 22×60 mm pitch, ~110×130 mm footprint. - **`render.sh`** + **`renders/`** — per-specimen iso PNG + STL, 3 X=0 cutaways (one per node size at mid gap = 0.3 mm), full-plate iso + STL, 2 contact-sheet montages. - **`README.md`** — DOE table, "what changed from the first revision" change log, IDEX (two-extruder) H2D / AMS-Pro-as-filament-store recipe, horizontal pull-test protocol with success criterion `F_pre` ∈ 5–25 N, and a forward note on the manual-threading alternative. ```scad // _common.scad — two knobs: joint size and air gap specimen_A3(id = "H-S1G2", node_d = 9.5, // axis 1: PLA node Ø (= bore length) gap_r = 0.3); // axis 2: radial air gap (mm) ``` ### Layout choices - **A3 countersunk** head (not A1 frustum): flush, self-centring, ~2.6× the bearing-wall area at the same OD. - **Horizontal cable orientation** — cable axis lies in the build plate (+Y) with the strut going up (+Z). The TPU has to bridge the bore horizontally as it extrudes, with gravity pulling it down into the air gap — i.e. intentional spaghetti / stringing across a short span. This is the real failure mode (the prior vertical-cable layout hid it). - **Single interface-treatment axis (air gap)** — the H2D is IDEX (two extruders), not three nozzles, and the AMS Pro 2 is a 4-slot filament store on the L extruder, so a sacrificial-PVA 3rd material is not available. Pause+lubricate is a manual workflow that doesn't survive a multi-specimen plate cleanly. Both were dropped from the first revision. - Self-contained directory; does **not** `include` from PR #39's `cad/joint-design/A_variants/`, so mergeable independently of #39. - The manual-elastic-threading alternative (no co-print needed) is captured in the README's "Notes / next steps" as a complementary path — this array remains useful for the co-printed-tendon direction (#54), where we still need to know the limiting air gap. ### Renders X=0 cross-sections (`section_montage.png`) show the bore + countersink + conical head at each node size. Issue #49 asked for best-practice guidance and applicable ASTM standards before the first round of Instron stiffness tests on the project's PETG-strut + TPU-85A-tendon multi-material FFF tensegrity-inspired cells, with explicit instruction to send a high-effort Edison query and fetch in-session.

### Changes

- **`scripts/edison/submit_instron_stiffness.py`** — submits one `LITERATURE_HIGH` task with a structured 7-section query (standards, protocol, checklist, stiffness-vs-EA campaign split, FFF data-quality, 5–15 analogs, equipment) anchored to the actual specimens; bounded ~28 min in-session poll; tolerant of `EDISON_API_KEY`/`EDISON_PLATFORM_API_KEY` shim and of `create_task` returning a bare `trajectory_id` string.
- **`edison-trajectories/instron-stiffness/`** — fetched outputs for task `9f68e71e-c552-4333-aa5c-37de18c8eefd` (status: success):
  - `*.md` (122 KB) — 16-row standards comparison, undergrad-runnable first-test checklist + metadata schema for the BO loop, 12 published analogs with DOIs (Bauer 2021, Pajunen 2019, Sabouni-Zawadzka 2024, Bates 2016, Solyaev 2023, Raghavendra 2021, Maskery 2015, Habib 2024, Pahari 2024, Lee 2020, Rossiter 2020, Arifvianto 2022).
  - `*.json` (2.2 MB) — raw `TaskResponseVerbose`.
  - `*.references.bib` — 81 unique BibTeX entries auto-extracted from the trajectory.
  - `README.md` — index + headline findings + recommended citation stack.
  - **`equipment-selection.md`** — maps the brief's recommendations onto the actually-available BYU CB 123 inventory (1 kip / 3 kip / 20 kip / 100 kip frames + MTS AOX optical extensometer) provided in PR feedback. Recommends the **1 kip Mini Tensile Tester + 100 lb load cell (≈ 445 N, ±1.1 N) + AOX** as the primary kit; defers the 3 kip / 20 kip / 100 kip frames as over-ranged for the small-strain regime.

### Recommended citation stack (from the brief)

> ASTM D638 + ASTM D412 + (ASTM D1621 *or* ASTM C365, adapted with deviations disclosed) + ASTM E111 + ASTM F2971 + ISO/ASTM 52900/52921; ISO 527 / ISO 37 / ISO 604 / ISO 13314 as recognized alternatives.

### Actionable items flagged before the first run

- The brief's "borrow / order a 100–500 N cell" recommendation is **resolved in-house** by the existing 100 lb cell on the 1 kip Mini Tensile Tester — no purchase needed.
- AOX (<2.5 µm res., 2 mm min gauge) directly satisfies the brief's non-contact-extensometer recommendation; gating item is the AOX training requirement.
- Run a steel-on-steel **machine-compliance** baseline on the 1 kip frame and subtract; use **AOX/DIC**, not crosshead, for sub-mm compliance.
- **5–10 TPU preconditioning cycles** for Mullins; report secant (not tangent) modulus over a stated strain window.
- Cap first monotonic loading **well below densification** (≤30 % strain); reserve full EA loading for the later campaign.
- Report **Gibson–Ashby** non-dimensionals (E\*/E\_s, ρ\*/ρ\_s) so single-cell and 2×2×2 tiled results are comparable.
- Add a **PETG–TPU joint-slip diagnostic** (DIC strain field on the joint) — peer-reviewed PETG–TPU interface data does not exist, so joint behavior must not be silently absorbed into a "material non-linearity" reading.
- Open equipment items: ASTM E4 calibration check on the 100 lb cell, AOX training slot, coupon dog-bone choice vs. the 6.35 mm width ceiling (likely D638 Type V + scaled D412 Die C), and steel-on-steel compliance platens sized for the 1 kip frame.

No production source, build, or test paths are touched.

body:
Issue asked to send an Edison Scientific query exploring an egg-drop demonstration on the PETG+TPU 85A tensegrity (how to secure the egg, mid-print pause feasibility, single cell vs tessellation vs ball, and instrumentation: high-speed video, embedded accelerometer, force-sensitive pad). PR comment 4413896231 then asked for a follow-up Edison query reframing the demo as a rooftop / no-drag drop that mimics a planetary-lander touchdown (PETG cradle inside the tensegrity), surveys the best drag-free egg protectors as a baseline, and proposes a V/m-constrained benchmark in which a tensegrity could be shown to win. PR comment 4427200746 then asked whether Keith Brown's lab's "superlative" energy-absorption geometry (BEAR self-driving lab) makes sense as a baseline, and a further in-session requirement asked Edison to clarify SUPERball v2's actuators (Vespignani 2018) and the tech-transfer implications of our passive, unactuated PETG+TPU tensegrity.

### Changes
- **`scripts/edison/submit_egg_drop.py`** — `LITERATURE_HIGH` submission covering pedagogy/novelty, egg fracture mechanics, securing trade-study (mid-print pause vs TPU harness vs external cradle, incl. food-safety), topology (cell/tessellation/icosahedron), instrumentation, and a 10-step protocol. Includes an `EDISON_API_KEY` → `EDISON_PLATFORM_API_KEY` shim since `edison-client ≥ 0.12` reads the latter (copilot-instructions still documents the old name).
- **`edison-trajectories/egg-drop-tensegrity-1b90208d.{md,json}`** — verbatim `formatted_answer` (with full numbered references) and structured `model_dump_json` for original task `1b90208d-3555-4479-9db0-512d67e69f5f`, fetched same-session per repo convention.
- **`scripts/edison/submit_egg_drop_followup.py`** — first follow-up `LITERATURE_HIGH` submission (PR comment 4413896231) covering (1) drag-free baseline survey across foam/lattice/spring/granular/tensegrity/bio-inspired protectors, (2) ranked best-in-class shortlist, (3) apples-to-apples benchmark protocol with shared V_max / m_sys constraints anchored on ASTM D5276 + F1292 + ISTA 1A + MIL-STD-810H 516.8, (4) regimes where the PETG+TPU tensegrity is expected to win (and where it is not), (5) recommended single-figure demo plot, and (6) reproducibility refs/parts list.
- **`edison-trajectories/egg-drop-followup-f41b7034.{md,json}`** — verbatim `formatted_answer` and `model_dump_json` for follow-up task `f41b7034-439e-45de-b97f-4bf1d85b9811`, fetched same-session.
- **`scripts/edison/submit_egg_drop_brown_lab.py`** — second follow-up `LITERATURE_HIGH` submission (PR comment 4427200746) on Keith Brown's lab BEAR / "superlative" energy absorber as a candidate baseline, covering (1) what was reported (Gongora 2020 *Sci. Adv.*, Gongora 2021 *iScience*, Gongora 2022 *Matter*, Snapp 2024 *Nat. Commun.*), (2) loading-regime applicability (quasi-static vs impact), (3) single-use vs reusable, (4) defensibility as the "BO-optimized lattice" baseline curve on the demo plot, (5) alternative impact-regime BO baselines, and (6) a one-paragraph recommendation.
- **`edison-trajectories/egg-drop-brown-lab-a3fc0429.{md,json}`** — verbatim `formatted_answer` and `model_dump_json` for follow-up task `a3fc0429-42ab-4a4b-ad8e-8e11574758a5`, fetched same-session.
- **`scripts/edison/submit_egg_drop_superball_actuators.py`** — third follow-up `LITERATURE_HIGH` submission (in-session requirement) on SUPERball v2's actuators (Vespignani 2018) and the passive-vs-actuated tech-transfer gap, covering (1) plain-English actuator description (type/mounting/stroke/role during landing vs locomotion), (2) contrast with our passive PETG+TPU tendons (incl. derived k for L=100 mm × Ø 3 mm TPU 85A), (3) tech-transfer limitations (preload uncertainty, fixed-k, no active landing, 2 m → 0.2 m scaling, reusability), (4) recommended design changes (motor-retrofit-ready hollow struts, dual-purpose anchors, instrumented tendons), (5) one-off validations (single-tendon force trace, k-sweep, pretension sensitivity, N-drop reusability, worst-case orientation, QS-vs-impact stiffness gap), and (6) bottom-line positioning recommendation.
- **`edison-trajectories/egg-drop-superball-actuators-f8f07966.{md,json}`** — verbatim `formatted_answer` and `model_dump_json` for follow-up task `f8f07966-2328-453a-900c-9903195af8a9`, fetched same-session.
- **`edison-trajectories/README.md`** — headline findings for the original task and the first follow-up + reproduction instructions. (Headline-findings bullets for the Brown-lab and SUPERball-v2 follow-ups were not added to the README due to time; full md/json artifacts and headline summaries are committed and linked from PR comment replies.)

### Headline answers — original task `1b90208d` (citations in the `.md`)
- **Novelty**: egg-drop pedagogy is well documented; no prior work uses a tensegrity as the cushion.
- **Securing the egg**: do **not** mid-print embed — PETG at 230 °C / 70 °C bed cooks the shell and biological contamination breaks layer adhesion. Use a **post-print TPU 85A cradle** integrated with the tendons; cling-film the egg for cleanup.
- **Topology**: six-bar tensegrity icosahedron. Zhang et al. 2018: 114.9 g (solid) → 40.9–46.5 g on a 1 m drop (~60–65 % peak-g reduction), inside the egg-survivable band. Bauer 2021 (~13× octet energy absorption, load-limiting plateau) and Pajunen 2019 (<0.2 % residual strain over 24+ impacts) corroborate.
- **Egg thresholds**: 24.6–53.5 N rupture force (Trnka 2012, weakest at equator), 2.3–6.1 mJ fracture energy; 50–150 g peak-deceleration heuristic.
- **Instrumentation**: ADXL375 (±200 g) on the cradle via ESP32 @ 3.2 kHz; piezo force plate (Kistler 9260AA / PCB 260A01) @ ≥ 10 kHz; ≥ 5 000 fps video with speckle/marker DIC; photogate-TTL sync across all three.
- **Protocol**: 0.25–2.0 m in 0.25 m steps, n ≥ 5 per height; expected survival transition 1.0–1.5 m; primary figure peak-g vs drop height with the 50–100 g survivability band overlaid (ASTM D5276 / F1292 framing).

### Headline answers — first follow-up task `f41b7034`
- **Best drag-free baselines**: Anand 2022 biodegradable tensegrity + coir survived 75 m (single-use); Agogino 2018 NASA SUPERball survived ~10 m egg drops <25 g, reusable; **Zhang 2022 22″ tensegrity** is the best instrumented reusable dataset (20 m drops, 235 g peak, ~20-drop life). Reusable elastic-foam baseline: TPU 95A honeycomb (Bates 2016 / Bustihan 2025). No formally standardized egg-drop benchmark exists in the peer-reviewed / planetary-lander literature; the SUPERball NIAC 1-foot-staircase egg-drop is the closest reusable analog and is the recommended adoption.
- **Apples-to-apples benchmark**: Ø 200 mm bounding sphere (V_max ≈ 4.19 × 10⁻³ m³), m_sys ≤ 500 g (protector + egg + sensors), m_egg = 55 ± 5 g, rigid concrete floor per ASTM D5276, both worst-case (vertex/face/edge) and random orientations. **Primary FoM**: h_crit (50 % survival, Bruceton up-down staircase, n ≥ 20, Δh = 0.5 m). **Secondary**: g_max@3 m (n = 5), SEA = E_abs/m_protector (J/g), η_V = E_abs/V_protector (J/cm³), N_reuse, m_protector/m_egg, V_protector/m_egg.
- **Where the tensegrity wins**: reusability under repeated impacts (Pajunen 2019: 24 impacts at 2.28 % residual; Bauer 2021: octet localizes >2.6 % strain, tensegrity stays >90 % delocalized), omnidirectionality (Zhang 2022: k = 7.0–15.4 kN/m across 3 orientations), and the low relative-density regime (Bauer 2021: 26× octet at ρ_rel < 4 %, 225× at 0.5 %). **Where it loses**: mass-critical *single-use* (foam densifies the whole volume, σ_yield ~9× tensegrity per Bauer 2021), volume-critical packaging (foam ~100 % active vs ~30–50 % stroke for a tensegrity shell), and very low drops (h < 2 m) where the cable network barely engages.
- **Recommended demo figure**: peak g vs drop height (0–15 m × 0–500 g) with the 130–300 g egg-fracture band shaded, comparing unprotected egg / TPU 95A honeycomb / EPS foam shell / PETG+TPU tensegrity, plus a companion N_reuse panel.

### Headline answers — Brown-lab BEAR follow-up task `a3fc0429`
- **What BEAR reported**: Gongora 2020 *Sci. Adv.* (4D crossed-barrel, toughness 0.3–51.5 J, ~60× faster than grid search), Gongora 2021 *iScience* (FEA-prior transfer learning), Gongora 2022 *Matter* (lattices for impact protection — title only retrievable), and **Snapp 2024 *Nat. Commun.*** (11D generalized cylindrical shells, 25 000+ physical experiments across 7 polymers; record **K_s = 75.2 % "Willow" PLA**, beating balsa 71.8 % and plastic foam 68.1 %; reusable TPU-2 "Iroko" K_s* ≈ 53 %).
- **Loading-regime mismatch**: every BEAR result is **quasi-static** (2–3 mm/min Instron, ε̇ ~10⁻³ s⁻¹), five to six orders of magnitude slower than a free-fall egg drop (ε̇ ~10²–10³ s⁻¹). Quasi-static rankings are *plausibly* preserved at moderate v_impact for type-I flat-plateau structures (Zhao 2005, Liu 2009) but **not experimentally validated**.
- **Reusability**: material-dependent. Record-holder is PLA, **single-use** (Willow flattens to ~23 % of original height); only TPU-2/TPE designs recover (~99 %, but K_s* ≈ 53 %).
- **Recommendation**: cite BEAR as conceptually-related prior art and frame the project as **"BEAR for tensegrities"** (apply the autonomous-BO methodology to the topologically distinct class-1 cable-strut design space). Only plot K_s as a baseline curve if the open-source GCS STL is re-printed and physically drop-tested under the f41b7034 protocol.

### Headline answers — SUPERball v2 actuator follow-up task `f8f07966`
- **Actuators**: plain-English description of SUPERball v2's 24 cable-driven actuators (type/mounting/stroke/role during landing vs locomotion).
- **Contrast with our passive tendons**: derived order-of-magnitude k for our TPU 85A tendons (L=100 mm × Ø 3 mm) for direct comparison against Vespignani's nylon ~4000 N/m / ~950 N peak.
- **Tech-transfer limitations**: cable preload uncertainty, inability to sweep k in situ, no active landing strategies, 2 m → 0.2 m scaling concerns (~10× higher strain rate, TPU rate dependence, Euler buckling), reusability.
- **Design changes**: motor-retrofit-ready hollow struts, dual-purpose anchors (passive TPU OR swaged cable termination), instrumented tendons (inline load cell or printed strain-gauge channel), pre-instrumented payload cradle.
- **One-off validations**: single-tendon force trace, cable-stiffness sensitivity sweep, pretension sensitivity, N-drop reusability test, worst-case orientation, quasi-static-vs-impact stiffness gap.
- **Bottom-line**: positioning recommendation for the passive PETG+TPU article as a scale-model precursor to actuated SUPERball-v2-class landers, with the minimum viable design changes and validations to support that framing in a future ASME JMD or RA-L submission.

### Reproducing
```bash
export EDISON_PLATFORM_API_KEY=...   # or EDISON_API_KEY (auto-mapped)
pip install edison-client
python scripts/edison/submit_egg_drop.py                         # original task 1b90208d
python scripts/edison/submit_egg_drop_followup.py                # follow-up task f41b7034
python scripts/edison/submit_egg_drop_brown_lab.py               # follow-up task a3fc0429
python scripts/edison/submit_egg_drop_superball_actuators.py     # follow-up task f8f07966
```

Issue asked: what is the right strut material for our PETG/TPU multi-material FDM tensegrity (PLA vs. PETG vs. HF-reinforced or other), via an Edison Scientific query whose results we then interpret. This PR submits the query, blocks for the result, commits all artifacts, and writes up the recommendation.

### Changes
- **`scripts/edison/submit_strut_material.py`** — `LITERATURE_HIGH` submission (blocking) scoped to our actual constraints (Bambu H2D, 0.4 mm nozzle, TPU 95A tendons, energy-absorption loading, ≥2 mm strut Ø). Compares PLA / PETG / CF-PLA / CF-PETG / continuous CF/Nylon / ABS / PC / PA-CF and disambiguates "HF-reinforced". Forwards `EDISON_API_KEY` → `api_key=` since `edison-client` only auto-reads `EDISON_PLATFORM_API_KEY`.
- **`edison-trajectories/strut-material-selection-5bb5e5d3-...{md,json,-references.md}`** — verbatim `formatted_answer` (47 KB, 38 cited refs w/ DOIs), full structured response, and extracted references section. Task `5bb5e5d3-b386-4ece-a894-9c87f0d67036`, status `success`. Edison returned no separate file artifacts for this task; everything is in those three files.
- **`edison-trajectories/strut-material-selection-summary.md`** — interpretation, ranked recommendation table, interface-evidence table, and proposed `references.bib` additions.

### Findings (TL;DR)
| Rank | Material | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **PLA** (keep baseline) | Only rigid/TPU pair with peer-reviewed bond data: PLA–TPU 6.5–7.4 MPa tensile, ~24 MPa shear w/ mechanical interlocking (Lopes 2018, Zhang 2026, Ruwais 2025). Highest neat-polymer stiffness → ~2× Euler buckling vs. PETG; best fatigue + UV. |
| 2 | **PETG** (Phase-2, conditional) | +20 °C HDT, more ductile, but **no peer-reviewed PETG–TPU bond number exists** — must be experimentally validated before adoption. |
| 3 | CF-PETG | Phase-2 only if buckling dominates; hardened nozzle, ~2× cost, no CF/TPU bond data. |
| — | Continuous CF/Nylon | Out of scope: not H2D-compatible, can't co-print TPU. |
| — | "HF-reinforced" = hemp-fiber PLA | Not competitive: impact drops 69.8 → 42.9 J/m, porosity 5.8 → 17.9%. |

**Novelty bonus:** no prior peer-reviewed work uses a PETG- (or fiber-reinforced-) strut + TPU-tendon tensegrity, so the proposed architecture is a publishable contribution as scoped. Action items for `proposal.tex` / `references.bib` are at the bottom of the summary file; this PR does not yet edit the proposal text.

I.e., search for funding opportunities (NSF, DOE, NIH, DOW, NASA, etc.) related to this. Use edison to help assist with this search.

Search for similar awards given by these various agencies, especially any and all funding related directly to tensegrity research.

Take into account Jeff's and my background, as well as a general leaning towards applied (at least knowing that we'll need some help framing things around the basic science rather than primarily on the application and end-use performance).

Take into consideration the potential directions of #16 and #18 and potentially other questions or topics for consideration. I'd prefer something longer-term, and if there's a timely call that's relevant, great, but I'm not as worried about rushing it so much as finding the right venue.

See other PRs (branches, comments, files) for additional context that might be needed.

- **`reviews/target_audience.md` (new)**
  - **§2 — Profile diversity.** Four sub-camps a JMD AE will recruit from (BO/data-driven design, architected/metamaterial mechanisms, AM/DfAM, biomechanics/assistive) with the major-revision risk each will flag. Calls out the impact-claim-overreach risk already raised by `reviews/mock_reviews.md`.
  - **§3a — Likely JMD Associate Editor coverage** by area, with named AEs / JMD-active researchers and representative JMD papers: Wei Chen (design optimization & data-driven design), Christopher Hoyle (BO in JMD), Pingfeng Wang (multi-fidelity), Faez Ahmed (generative/AI-assisted design), James Allison (design automation), Larry Howell / Pooya Sareh (compliant/origami — Howell flagged as BYU COI), David Rosen / Levent Kara (DfAM).
  - **§3b — 14 named candidate reviewers**, each anchored to ≥1 paper in JMD or a directly relevant peer-reviewed venue (Composite Structures, Adv. Mater., Sci. Adv., Addit. Manuf., Extreme Mech. Lett., npj Comput. Mater., S&MO, J. Eng. Mech., J. Mech. Robotics, J. Appl. Mech.): Rimoli, Valdevit, Fraternali, Pajunen, Santos, Micheletti, Peraza Hernandez (tensegrity & architected metamaterials); Liwei Wang, Vangelatos, Sheikh, Mo, Khatamsaz, Ahmed (BO for materials/structures, all journal-publishing); Hertlein (impact/AM optimization).
  - **§3c — COI screen** with hard exclusions (Larry Howell, Brian Jensen — both BYU) and the standard 4-year ASME COI window for the rest.
  - **§3d — SMS backup-venue analog**: Santos, Fraternali, Micheletti, Pajunen, Sabouni-Zawadzka; framing pivot guidance (lead with novel metamaterial behavior and tunable energy absorption rather than the BO workflow).
  - **§3d′ — "Lander"-style designs / drag-free impact survival contacts** (added in response to PR comment 4427225555 referencing PR #47): a 10-row ranked outreach table grounded in PR #47's Edison trajectories `egg-drop-tensegrity-1b90208d.md` and `egg-drop-followup-f41b7034.md`. Suggested first-contact set of 3: **Julian J. Rimoli** (Georgia Tech — *On the impact tolerance of tensegrity-based planetary landers*, AIAA SciTech 2016), **Adrian K. Agogino** (NASA Ames — NIAC SUPERball Phase 2 final report 2018, the only published egg-payload tensegrity drop with quantitative deceleration data), **Mark W. Mueller** (UC Berkeley HiPeRLab — Zha et al., *IEEE/ASME Trans. Mechatronics* 2024 collision-resilient icosahedron). Tier-2 (4–10): Vytas SunSpiral, Andrew Zhang + Brian Cera (UC Berkeley, Agogino lineage), Massimo Vespignani (SUPERball v2), Skelton/Sultan, Jamshid Bayandor (Virginia Tech CRASH Lab — TANDEM 2017), Jing Zhang et al. (HIT — *Aerospace* 2025), Madhumati Anand (biodegradable tensegrity, 75 m drops). Extensively explore and validate joint design for PETG/PLA (struts) + TPU (cables) prints meant to mimic tensegrity.

## Edison query batch

- Fetched + committed Edison trajectories `1400ca69` (commercial-tensegrity collaborators) and `3b9d76b5` (academic venues) → `edison-trajectories/{1400ca69…,3b9d76b5…}.{md,json}`.
- Surveyed existing joint context across the repo (issues #28, #33, #37; PRs #22, #24, #35) and distilled 5 candidate joint design ideas grounded in the H2D PETG+TPU IDEX print stack and the in-progress single-piece T3-prism (PR #35).
- **Stage 1** — submitted one **1-credit `LITERATURE` Edison query per joint design idea** (5 total) with proposal/CAD/literature/equipment context attached; all 5 fetched + committed (md+json):
  - `A-anchor-bulb` task `0b5d7ba2…`
  - `B-dovetail` task `ccb7b854…`
  - `C-tpu-sleeve-overmold` task `5a7ffce4…`
  - `D-eyelet-loop` task `727a449d…`
  - `E-tpu-rebar` task `ae373eb5…`
- **Stage 2 in tandem** — `LITERATURE_HIGH be6768ab…` (prior-art ranking) + `ANALYSIS c38a2046…` (synthesis + design-for-test recommendation) — both fetched + committed (md+json).
- Submitted follow-up `ANALYSIS ce84ddf8-5930-4c61-a6ce-65cf9ee3a6fa` with **all 5** Phase-1 outputs attached (the original `c38a2046` only had C/D/E because A and B finished after submission). Fetched + committed: it **inverts** the recommendation to **B (dovetail) primary + A (anchor-bulb) backup** — the prior-art quantitative gap (Ermolai 2024 / Zhang 2021 reporting 6–24 MPa for FDM dovetails vs. Yavas 2022 1–2.7 MPa for the rebar-shear analog) outweighed E's theoretical simplicity.
- Synthesis `edison-trajectories/joint-design/README.md` links every artifact, contrasts the two Phase-2 rankings, and surfaces the original recommendation. `task_manifest.json` records every submitted task ID, its attachments, and its status.

## OpenSCAD CAD models, renders, and visual prior-art comparison

- Authored OpenSCAD CAD models for **all 5** candidate joints under `cad/joint-design/`: `A_anchor_bulb.scad`, `B_dovetail.scad`, `C_tpu_sleeve_overmold.scad`, `D_eyelet_loop.scad`, `E_tpu_rebar.scad`, plus per-design **three-orthogonal-plane** cutaway variants `*_section_{X,Y,Z}.scad` and a shared `_common.scad` parameter file. Initial geometry followed the Phase-2 ANALYSIS recommendations.
- `cad/joint-design/render.sh` produces iso + section PNG renders + STL exports for each design and assembles four contact-sheet montages: `renders/all_iso_montage.png`, `renders/all_section_montage.png` (Y-cut row), `renders/all_compare_montage.png` (CAD-vs-reference side-by-side), and `renders/all_multiplane_section_montage.png` (4×5 grid: iso + 3 orthogonal cuts × 5 designs).
- Curated **public reference images** for visual prior-art comparison at `cad/joint-design/references/README.md` — verified-200 Wikimedia Commons URLs (tensegrity 3-prism, finished dovetail joint, hose clamp, chain-link fence, rebar loop, anchor-bolt SVG, etc.) plus DOIs of the closest peer-reviewed prior-art papers (Pajunen 2019, Ermolai 2024, Zhang 2021, Khatri 2024, Yavas 2022, Mortensen 2025). 5 reference JPEGs downloaded locally and resized.

## Phase-3 follow-up Edison ANALYSIS (CAD review against published prior art) — fetched + applied

- Submitted Edison **`ANALYSIS 19e0c868-3587-440d-ba4a-07da4dddf99a`** attaching the zipped `cad/joint-design/` directory (5 SCAD + section variants + 13 PNG renders + 5 STL + 3 montages + references README + 5 reference JPEGs), the `ce84ddf8` followup, the joint-design synthesis README, and `task_manifest.json`.
- Submission script committed at `scripts/edison/submit_joint_cad_review.py`; submission record (task ID + every attached `data_entry:` URI) at `edison-trajectories/joint-design/PHASE3-cad-review-SUBMITTED.json`.
- **Phase-3 result fetched + committed** at `edison-trajectories/joint-design/PHASE3-cad-review-19e0c868-3587-440d-ba4a-07da4dddf99a.{md,json}`. `task_manifest.json` `phase3.cad_review` updated to `success`.
- **Applied Phase-3 dimensional refinements to `B_dovetail.scad` (uni-axial primary)**:
  - `node_d` 9.0 → **12.0 mm** (≥2-perimeter PETG cheek)
  - `slot_mouth` 6.4 → **5.4 mm**, `slot_inner` 7.4 → **7.06 mm**, `slot_height` 3.6 → **4.0 mm**, `slot_depth` 5.0 → **6.0 mm**
  - `flank_deg` 25 → **22.5°** (Wang 2026 shear optimum)
  - Differential clearance: `clear_lat` **0.20 mm** (Y, load-bearing), `clear_roof` **0.30 mm** (Z, bridge sag) — Ermolai 2024
  - `mouth_fillet` **0.5 mm** (Frascio 2024 TPU de-notch)
- **Applied Phase-3 refinements to `A_anchor_bulb.scad` (lander/egg-drop primary; uni-axial backup)**:
  - `node_d` 9.0 → **9.5 mm**, `bore_d` 2.9 → **2.8 mm**, `bulb_d` 4.0 → **4.8 mm** (raises pull-through ratio 1.38× → **1.71×**)
- Re-ran `cad/joint-design/render.sh` → updated iso + section PNGs, STLs, and all four contact-sheet montages to reflect the refined B and A geometry.
- Updated synthesis README (`edison-trajectories/joint-design/README.md`) with a Phase-3 row + parameter-change tables.

## Multi-plane cross-section pass + visualization bug fixes (per PR review feedback)

- Added per-design orthogonal cross-section `.scad` files at three cut planes (Y=0, X=0, Z=−2): `A_anchor_bulb_section_{X,Y,Z}.scad`, `B_dovetail_section_{X,Y,Z}.scad`, `C_tpu_sleeve_overmold_section_{X,Y,Z}.scad`, `D_eyelet_loop_section_{X,Y,Z}.scad`, `E_tpu_rebar_section_{X,Y,Z}.scad`.
- Generating these cuts surfaced two non-physical visualizations in the prior CAD, which were fixed:
  - **`B_dovetail.scad`**: TPU cable was emerging at z=0 while the dovetail head was centered at z=−3.5 — cable was floating in air, disconnected from the head. Cable now exits the +X face of the node along the slot centerline and is mechanically continuous with the head.
  - **`D_eyelet_loop.scad`**: refactored `designD()` into `designD_petg()` / `designD_tpu()` modules and clarified the eyelet-center geometry (`eyelet_center_z` constant) so the chain-link topology (linking number ±1) is visibly unambiguous from any of the three cut planes.
- New `cad/joint-design/renders/all_multiplane_section_montage.png` assembles iso + 3 cuts × 5 designs into a 4×5 grid for at-a-glance topology verification.

## Lander/egg-drop (#16) and PLA (#45) integration

- Added a "Lander-context recommendation" section to the synthesis README: for the omnidirectional-impact, n≥20-Bruceton-drop egg-drop / planetary-lander demo (issue #16), the recommended joint is **A (anchor-bulb)** with the Phase-3-refined geometry. **B (co-printed dovetail / T-slot)** remains the recommended joint for the **uni-axial crutch-tip print**.
- Documented that the strut material is now planned to be **PLA per #45**, not PETG.

## Phase-4 Edison submissions (per PR review feedback) — non-blocking, fetch next session

- **`LITERATURE_HIGH f9804247-51f3-43de-a676-94b4b008b886` — project-context single-joint pick.** Asks Edison to recommend one joint design (A–E) given the full project context: PLA struts per #45, TPU 85A tendons, lander/egg-drop demo per #16 (Bruceton n≥20, omnidirectional impact, reusability), Bambu H2D IDEX print stack, and the Phase-3-refined geometry for A and B.
- **`ANALYSIS e9a1f4cc-7509-41b4-89e7-3f63ef406333` — per-design vision review with individual tiles.** Attaches **27 individual files** (5 `.scad` sources + 5 iso PNGs + 15 `section_{X,Y,Z}` PNGs + `_common.scad` + the joint-design README) — explicitly **no mosaics** — and specifically asks for confirmation of B-dovetail slot-axis cable continuity and D-eyelet chain-link topology.
- Submission script: `scripts/edison/submit_joint_phase4.py`. Submission records (task IDs + every attached `data_entry:` URI): `edison-trajectories/joint-design/PHASE4-{context,vision}-SUBMITTED.json`. `task_manifest.json` extended with a `phase4` section.

## Anchor-upset shape variants (per PR review feedback)

In response to the question of why design A uses a sphere, authored CAD + visualizations for **5 alternative TPU upset shapes** for design A, all preserving the Phase-3 1.71× pull-through ratio (only the upset shape changes):

- **A0** — spherical (reference baseline; matches `A_anchor_bulb.scad`)
- **A1** — truncated cone / frustum (rivet head; flat bearing face for cleaner top-layer finish)
- **A2** — torus / donut (distributes bearing load over a wider annulus, lower peak contact stress)
- **A3** — conical countersunk head (flush, self-centering, ~8.8 mm² conical wall)
- **A4** — 6-lobed / star / knurled head (rotational keying for Bruceton n≥20 reuse)
- **A5** — mushroom / tee-head with 0.4 mm radiused undercut (Frascio 2024; maximum mechanical interlock per gram of TPU)

## Design F — captive TPU core inside PETG/PLA outer shell

New **Design F** (`cad/joint-design/F_captive_core.scad`) — a non-feed-through anchor in which the TPU "knot" lives entirely inside a PETG/PLA outer shell:

- Ø7 mm TPU captive core inside Ø12 mm shell (Ø8 mm cavity, 0.5 mm radial print-in-place gap) — **pull-out ratio 2.5×** vs. 1.71× for Phase-3 A.
- **Teardrop strut→shell fillet** via convex hull — smooth blend, no stress riser.
- **Layer-interlock teeth (per @achris0520)** — two staggered rings of 8 radial teeth (PETG inward at z=+0.6 mm, TPU outward at z=−0.6 mm, 22.5° rotational stagger) so the captive core cannot translate ±Z without relying on PETG/PLA-TPU chemical adhesion.

## Proposal correction — removed unverified Ye et al. tensegrity attribution

Edison Phase-5 ANALYSIS (`28d942ea`) confirmed that the `ye2023multimaterial` citation (Ye et al. 2023, *Nature Communications* — thick-panel origami metamaterials) does not describe a tensegrity core-wrapping strategy, and the DOI previously associated with the claim resolved to an unrelated paper (Filla et al., fibrin-fibre networks). Additionally, the description was topologically inverted relative to the actual project design (which uses a captive TPU core **inside** a PLA shell, not PLA struts encapsulated by TPU skins).

Removed all three occurrences of the incorrect attribution from `proposal.tex`:

- **Background ¶** — deleted the "wrapping-based strategy (rigid cores encapsulated by continuous soft skins)" sentence; retained the PLA–TPU energy-absorption claim citing `khatri2024energy` alone.
- **Intro ¶** — dropped `ye2023multimaterial` from the multi-material fabrication citation.
- **Section 1** — removed the "Following \citet{ye2023multimaterial}, the designs use a core-wrapping strategy (rigid PLA struts encapsulated by continuous TPU skins)…" sentence entirely.

`proposal.pdf` and `proposal-diff.pdf` rebuilt to reflect the correction.
