body:
## T3-prism slicing fixes (PR #35 comment 4464399849)

- Diagnosed "only PLA shown": `Metadata/project_settings.config` had `filament_colour=['#00AE42']` and `filament_map=['1']` (length 1) but `filament_settings_id`/`filament_type` had length 2 — Bambu Studio uses the shorter array length to determine filament count, so it imported as single-material PLA.
- Diagnosed "floating supports": scaffold pillars started at SCAD `z=0` but the lowest model point is the joint-sphere bottom at SCAD `z=-joint_d/2 = -5.25 mm` (scale 1.5). When Bambu lifted the assembly so the lowest point sat on the bed, the pillars floated ~5.25 mm above it.
- Fix 1: `patch_mm_extruder.py` now also patches `Metadata/project_settings.config` — pads `filament_colour` from a default extruder palette and `filament_map` with ascending extruder IDs to match `filament_settings_id` length, and switches `filament_map_mode` to `Manual` so Bambu Studio honours the per-extruder routing.
- Fix 2: in `t3-prism.scad` `pillar_to()`, drop pillar bases to SCAD `z=-joint_d/2` so they reach the bed when the assembled model sits on it (matches the lowest point of the struts/joints).
- Re-rendered STLs and re-ran `render_print.sh` end-to-end → all 3 MM project `.3mf`s now show `filament_colour=['#00AE42','#76D9F4']`, `filament_map=['1','2']`, `filament_map_mode=Manual`; scaffold STL z-range now `[-1.75, 113.74]` matching the struts STL exactly.
- Re-rendered `t3-prism.H2D-PETG-supports.png` verification render.

## T3-prism Sobol BO single-batch generator (PR #35 comment 4503109338)

- Added `bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py`, a Honegumi/Ax-style adaptation of PR #30 `bo/tensegrity_campaign.py` that generates a single batch of T3-prism-only Sobol specimens (no model fit, no `complete_trial` — human-in-the-loop, one iteration only).
- Swept design variables (T3-prism-specific, per PRs #24 / #30): `R_mm`, `H_mm`, `twist_deg`, `strut_d_mm`, `cable_d_mm`.
- Frozen for this batch: `topology=t3_prism`, `tiling=1x1x1`, `build_orientation=vertical`, `tpu_shore=85A`, PLA struts / TPU cables, supports = manual-painted (@achris0520 paints), `joint_d=7 mm`.
- Packs 9 specimens (3×3 grid) vertically on the H2D 350×320 mm plate; each specimen rooted so the bottom joint-sphere underside sits on the bed.
- Emits `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch.{csv,json,scad,stl}` and `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch-{plate,iso}.png` previews for spot-checking before importing to Bambu Studio.
- `bo/README.md` documents the swept vs. frozen variables and run instructions.

## BO batch multi-material project `.3mf` (PR #35 comment 4503267471)

- "Split to parts" in Bambu Studio was producing a single object because the BO batch SCAD unioned struts and cables into one mesh and the generator only wrote a single combined STL.
- Refactored `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch.scad` to expose per-specimen `specimen_NN_struts()` / `specimen_NN_cables()` modules and a top-level `part = "all" | "struts" | "cables"` switch, mirroring the `cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad` pattern used by the working `t3-prism-separate-assembly.zip` reference.
- `bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py` now renders `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch-struts.stl` and `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch-cables.stl` as separate STLs (one per material), in addition to the combined preview STL.
- Wired the BambuStudio CLI `--assemble` path into the BO script to produce `bo/slices/t3-prism-bo-batch.H2D-MM-PLAstruts-TPUcables.3mf` with PLA struts on extruder 1 (`Bambu PLA Basic @BBL H2D`), TPU 85A cables on extruder 2 (`Bambu TPU 85A @BBL H2D 0.4 nozzle`), and no auto-supports (manual-painting workflow). A `--skip-mm-3mf` flag is available for SCAD/STL-only runs.
- Verified the MM project: `filament_settings_id=['Bambu PLA Basic @BBL H2D','Bambu TPU 85A @BBL H2D 0.4 nozzle']`, `filament_type=['PLA','TPU']`, `filament_colour=['#00AE42','#76D9F4']`, `filament_map=['1','2']`, `filament_map_mode=Manual`; `Metadata/model_settings.config` routes the struts STL to extruder 1 and the cables STL to extruder 2 — *Split to parts* now exposes both as independently-assignable parts.
- Updated `bo/README.md` to document the new struts/cables STLs, the MM project `.3mf`, and the `--skip-mm-3mf` flag.

## BO batch tighter plate spacing (PR #35 comment 4503427854)

- Tightened the 3×3 plate packing in `bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py` by dropping the `strut_d` term from the per-specimen footprint estimate and reducing the inter-cell air gap from 5 mm → 2 mm.
- Grid cell shrinks from 97.0 mm → 86.9 mm per axis (~30 mm tighter overall on the 350×320 mm H2D plate) while still keeping each specimen's bounding cylinder inside its cell.
- Regenerated `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch.{scad,stl,json,csv}`, `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch-{struts,cables}.stl`, `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch-{plate,iso}.png`, and `bo/slices/t3-prism-bo-batch.H2D-MM-PLAstruts-TPUcables.3mf` end-to-end.

## Captive TPU core inside PLA outer shell joints (PR #35 comment 4511036510)

- Replaced solid joint spheres at every T3-prism vertex with a **captive TPU core inside a hollow PLA outer shell** (per PR #39 comment 4461700096 / Design F adapted to a 3-cable junction):
  - **PLA outer shell** (`joint_shell()` in `cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad`): hollow sphere with a teardrop hull blend toward the strut and one cylindrical exit bore per outgoing TPU cable (3 per joint).
  - **TPU captive core** (`joint_core()` in `cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad`): solid sphere inside the cavity, continuous with the cable end-caps emerging through the bores.
  - Print-in-place clearance: `bore = cable_d + 0.8 mm`, `core_od ≥ bore + 3 mm` (TPU mass cannot back out any single bore), `shell_id = core_od + 1 mm`, `shell_od = shell_id + 3.2 mm` PLA wall.
  - `use_captive_core` toggle in `t3-prism.scad` (default `true`) preserves the legacy solid-joint path for direct comparison.
- Mirrored the captive-core joint verbatim in the BO batch generator (`bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py` `SPECIMEN_TEMPLATE`) so every per-specimen joint is also captive-core, with per-specimen `cable_d`-derived shell/core/bore sizing.
- Updated `render_print.sh` `offset_z` (3.5 → 8.15 mm), `pillar_to()`, and `bo/specimen_footprint()` / `z_lift` so the now-lower PLA shell underside lands on the bed and the per-specimen plate-grid cell accommodates the (larger) shell OD.
- Re-rendered `cad/t3-prism/{t3-prism, t3-prism-struts, t3-prism-cables, t3-prism-struts-scaffold}.stl` + `t3-prism-iso.png`, and `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch{.scad, .csv, .json, .stl, -struts.stl, -cables.stl, -plate.png, -iso.png}`.
- Documented the captive-core joint geometry, clearance rationale, and `use_captive_core` toggle in `cad/t3-prism/README.md` and `bo/README.md`.

## TPU misalignment with joints

- Diagnosed: previously `cables.stl` lowest world-Z was `-cable_d/2` while `struts.stl` lowest was `-max(strut_d, joint_d)/2`; Bambu Studio's per-part auto-bed-placement therefore dropped the cables vs. the struts by ~3 mm — exactly the reported "horizontal cables going to the wrong z-height on the top and bottom".
- Fixed by giving `cables.stl` the same world-Z bounding box as `struts.stl`:
  - The new captive TPU core spheres at every joint vertex naturally extend the cables-STL bbox to `±core_od/2`.
  - Plus a 5 µm × 5 µm axial spike (`cables_z_anchor()` in `t3-prism.scad`, equivalent inline cube in the BO `SPECIMEN_TEMPLATE`) that pins the cables STL bbox to exactly the struts STL extents.
- Verified at scale 1.5×: `t3-prism-struts.stl` z=[0.017, 121.283] vs `t3-prism-cables.stl` z=[0.000, 121.300] — sub-mm match. Verified for BO batch: `struts.stl` z=[0.068, 116.925] vs `cables.stl` z=[-0.000, 117.072] — sub-mm match across all 9 specimens.

## BO batch plate spacing + prime tower reserve (PR #35 comments 4513164299 / 4513445377)

- Added a reserved strip on +X of the H2D plate for the IDEX prime/flush tower (`PRIME_TOWER_RESERVE_X`), drawn as a thin slab marker in the preview SCAD only (not into the struts/cables STLs).
- First pass dropped to 6 specimens in a 3×2 layout with a 12 mm air gap and 70 mm reserve; per follow-up feedback ("keep it to 3×3"), reverted `N_SPECIMENS` back to **9** in a **3×3 grid** with a **6 mm** inter-cell air gap and a **50 mm** prime-tower reserve strip on +X, keeping the layout inside the 300×320 mm usable plate area while leaving room for the wipe tower.
- Regenerated `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch.{scad,stl,json,csv}`, `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch-{struts,cables}.stl`, `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch-{plate,iso}.png`, and `bo/slices/t3-prism-bo-batch.H2D-MM-PLAstruts-TPUcables.3mf` end-to-end.
- Added `bo/__pycache__/` to `.gitignore`.

## Bonded captive-core joints + per-specimen object grouping (PR #35 comment 4513722886)

Addressing three asks from @sgbaird:

- **TPU members connect at every vertex** — the captive TPU core sphere at each vertex unions all three cable end-cap spheres + cable cylinders into one continuous TPU mass.
- **Full spherical PLA shell around each TPU vertex** with no gaps except cable bores, in contact with the TPU core so the materials bond:
  - Dropped the teardrop hull blend toward the strut (every vertex shell is now a uniform sphere — consistent across all six vertices).
  - `captive_core_clear = 0` so the TPU core touches the PLA inner wall (was a 0.5 mm radial print-in-place gap → now bonded).
  - `captive_bore_clear = 0` so the PLA bore is exactly `cable_d` and the TPU cable fills it without an annular gap (was 0.4 mm/side).
  - Mirrored the same captive-core geometry in `bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py` `SPECIMEN_TEMPLATE`.
- **Each tensegrity iteration on the plate is its own Bambu Studio object with two part groups (PLA + TPU)** — `bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py` now:
  - Adds a `spec=-1` filter to the generated batch SCAD so individual specimens can be rendered (`-D spec=N`).
  - Renders per-specimen STLs into `bo/per-specimen-stls/t3-prism-bo-specNN-{struts,cables}.stl` (one pair per specimen).
  - Passes all 2N STLs to BambuStudio `--assemble` and post-processes the resulting `.3mf` with a new `_split_assembled_into_objects()` helper that splits the single composite into N composite objects, each containing one struts part (extruder 1 / PLA) and one cables part (extruder 2 / TPU). Objects are not grouped; each can be moved independently while its PLA + TPU parts move together.
  - Verified in `bo/slices/t3-prism-bo-batch.H2D-MM-PLAstruts-TPUcables.3mf`: 9 `<object>` entries, each with two `<part>`s (struts→ext1, cables→ext2); 9 `<model_instance>` entries on the plate; `filament_type=['PLA','TPU']`, `filament_map_mode=Manual`, `filament_map=['1','2']`.
- Re-rendered `cad/t3-prism/{t3-prism, t3-prism-struts, t3-prism-cables, t3-prism-struts-scaffold}.stl` + iso PNG, re-assembled `cad/t3-prism/slices/t3-prism.H2D{,-PETG,-PETG.gcode,-MM,-MM-PLAcables,-MM-PLAstruts-TPUcables}.3mf`, re-rendered `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch-{plate,iso}.png` + `bo/t3-prism-bo-batch{,-struts,-cables}.stl` + the 18 per-specimen STLs.
- Updated `cad/t3-prism/README.md` and `bo/README.md` to document the bonded captive-core geometry and the per-specimen object grouping.

## Accelerometer "igloo" mount on top vertices (PR #35 comment 4794790065)

Addressing @sgbaird's request to extrude a block on top of the top vertices with a pocket to secure the 3-axis accelerometer:

- Added a parametric accelerometer mount to `cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad` (`accel_mount()` / `accel_mount_local()`, plus `accel_*` parameters and helper functions) fused onto each of the **three top vertices**:
  - Pocket sized to the **Dytran 3133A4** accelerometer (measured **6 × 6 × 5.94 mm** L×W×H, per PR #74 comment 4792400480), with `accel_clear` = 0.4 mm/side clearance for the adhesive bead and slide-in fit. Because the accelerometer is a physical part, its dimensions are absolute mm and are **not** multiplied by `scale_factor`.
  - **Three walls + a floor and one open outward-facing front** so the sensor slides in from the side and its cable feeds out horizontally.
  - A rounded **"igloo" crown** (`accel_dome`) over the pocket to reduce friction against the acrylic drop-test plate.
  - The mount is PLA and is unioned into `t3_prism_struts()`, so it routes to extruder 1 in the MM variant. Toggleable via `add_accel_mount` (default `true`).
  - Extended `cables_z_anchor()` by `accel_rise()` so the cables STL bounding box still matches the now-taller struts STL (verified sub-mm parity).
- Re-rendered `cad/t3-prism/{t3-prism, t3-prism-struts, t3-prism-cables, t3-prism-struts-scaffold}.stl` + `t3-prism-iso.png`, and regenerated all `cad/t3-prism/slices/*.3mf` end-to-end via `render_print.sh` (BambuStudio CLI v02.06.00.51).
- Documented the mount geometry, parameters, and igloo rationale in `cad/t3-prism/README.md`.

## Accelerometer mount: flat seat above joint apex + 0.2 mm tolerances (PR #35 comment 4805516634)

Addressing @sgbaird's feedback that the joint underneath was poking through the pocket so the accelerometer could not sit flat, and the request to change the tolerances to 0.2 mm top / 0.2 mm bottom:

- **Flat pocket floor that clears the joint for all designs by default**: the pocket floor was previously sunk *below* the joint apex (at `apex − 0.5 mm`), so the rounded captive-core joint shell poked up into the pocket. `accel_mount()` now places the pocket floor a full `accel_floor` (1.5 mm) **above** the joint apex `V[2] + joint_outer_r()`, while `accel_mount_local()` extends the body underside to `-(accel_floor + accel_sink)` so the walls still sink `accel_sink` (2 mm) past the apex and stay fused to the joint. Because the seat height is derived from `joint_outer_r()` (which tracks `cable_d` / `scale_factor`), the floor clears the joint apex for every design and scale by default (verified at scale 1.5×: top-vertex apex z=112.65 < pocket floor z=114.15; struts STL z=[0.52, 131.63] vs cables STL z=[0.50, 131.64] — sub-mm parity preserved).
- **0.2 mm top / 0.2 mm bottom Z tolerances**: added `accel_clear_top` and `accel_clear_bot` (0.2 mm each) for the pocket depth (`accel_pocket_z() = accel_h + accel_clear_top + accel_clear_bot`); the 0.4 mm lateral (XY) slide-in fit `accel_clear` is unchanged. Updated `accel_rise()` to drop the `accel_sink` term accordingly.
- Re-rendered `cad/t3-prism/{t3-prism, t3-prism-struts, t3-prism-cables, t3-prism-struts-scaffold}.stl` + `t3-prism-iso.png`, regenerated all `cad/t3-prism/slices/*.3mf` end-to-end via `render_print.sh` (BambuStudio CLI; single-material sliced job `return_code=0`, 2.90 h / 34.87 g; MM project `filament_type=['PLA','TPU']`, `filament_map_mode=Manual`, `filament_map=['1','2']`), and re-rendered `t3-prism.H2D-PETG-supports.png`.
- Documented the flat-floor seat geometry and the new top/bottom tolerance parameters in `cad/t3-prism/README.md`.

## Accelerometer mount: fill the outer void / remove the overhanging lip (PR #35 comment 4813200802)

Addressing @sgbaird's feedback that there was an outer void under the igloo that should be filled by extruding from the surface below up to the underside of the igloo, removing the lip around the edge that could be a stress point:

- **Diagnosed the void**: the igloo body's flat rectangular underside is wider than the rounded joint beneath it, so its rim overhung an unsupported gap — a thin lip / stress riser that could crack.
- **Added a skirt to `accel_mount()`** that convex-hulls the body's underside footprint down onto the joint sphere, so PLA runs continuously from the joint surface up to the underside of the igloo (void filled, overhanging lip removed). Because it is derived from `joint_outer_r()`, this is correct for **every** design/scale by default.
- The skirt re-applies the joint shell's cavity (`captive_shell_id`) and cable-bore cuts — the bores are lengthened so they always punch through the thicker fillet wall — so the captive TPU core and the three cable exits stay open. Struts STL volume topology is unchanged (manifold) and struts/cables world-Z parity is preserved (struts z=[0.516, 131.631] vs cables z=[0.500, 131.640]).
- `accel_mount()` now takes the per-vertex `cable_dirs` so the call site passes `vertex_cable_dirs_t(i)`.
- Re-rendered `cad/t3-prism/{t3-prism, t3-prism-struts, t3-prism-cables, t3-prism-struts-scaffold}.stl` + `t3-prism-iso.png`, regenerated all `cad/t3-prism/slices/*.3mf` end-to-end via `render_print.sh` (MM project `filament_type=['PLA','TPU']`, `filament_map=['1','2']`, `filament_map_mode=Manual`), and re-rendered `t3-prism.H2D-PETG-supports.png`.
- Documented the skirt / void-fill geometry in `cad/t3-prism/README.md`.

body: Three struts in a triangle. They all rotate at 60 degrees. Top is also a triangle, rotated. From bottom to top is a "string". https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tensegrity > The simplest tensegrity structure (a T3-prism). Each of three compression members (green) is symmetric with the other two, and symmetric from end to end. Each end is connected to three cables (red), which provide tension and precisely define the position of that end in the same way as the three cables in the [Skylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skylon_(Festival_of_Britain)) define the bottom end of its tapered pillar. Assume pure PETG for now, not multi-material Get the STL file too, just in case. Take into heavy consideration: https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/powder-doser/pull/7, for example, you might choose to use QueryCad. We had some success related to programmatic CAD in https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/powder-doser/pull/16

body:
Repo had no BO code yet. Added a `honegumi`-driven scaffold for the multi-material tensegrity energy-absorption campaign so we have a runnable Ax/BoTorch starting point to iterate on, plus a hand-customized companion script that wires up the real design variables and objectives drawn from `proposal.tex`, `idetc-abstract.tex`, `nasa-space-grant/proposal.tex`, and PR #24.

### `bo/` layout
- **`generate_scaffold.py`** — wraps `honegumi.core._honegumi.Honegumi`, declares `CONFIG`, renders `tensegrity_bo.py`. `--smoke-test` overrides honegumi's `dummy` flag for a 5-iter variant (honegumi's public `generate()` always forces `dummy=False`).
- **`tensegrity_bo.py`** — generated, `black`-formatted Ax loop; Branin placeholder objective is intentionally left for replacement per the customization checklist.
- **`tensegrity_campaign.py`** — hand-customized Ax MOO campaign companion to the regenerable scaffold. Flat top-to-bottom script (no `main()`, no `__main__` guard, no CLI) — tune the `N_ITERATIONS` / `BATCH_SIZE` / `SEED` module-level constants in place. Design space now tracks the PETG-strut + TPU-skin recommendations from PR #24's Edison literature scoping:
  - **Continuous**: strut diameter `[1.5, 5.0] mm`, strut length `[15, 50] mm`, TPU cable diameter `[1.0, 3.0] mm`, twist angle `[10°, 45°]`, prestress `[0%, 5%]`, PETG infill `[40%, 100%]`, interface wrap thickness `[0.4, 2.0] mm`.
  - **Integer (ordered choice)**: struts per unit cell ∈ `{3, 4, 6, 8, 12}`.
  - **Categorical**: connectivity topology ∈ `{truncated_octahedron, simplex_4_strut, t3_prism, stacked_prism}` (the four "defensible seed families" from PR #24), tiling ∈ `{1×1×1, 1×1×2, 2×2×1, 2×2×2, 3×3×2}`, TPU shore ∈ `{85A, 95A}`, PETG infill pattern ∈ `{rectilinear, grid, gyroid}`, build orientation ∈ `{vertical, horizontal, 45°}`.
  - **Objectives** (MOO / qNEHVI): minimize `F_peak_N`, maximize `SEA_J_per_g`, maximize `eta`.

  Exploration is handled by Ax's default `GenerationStrategy` (Sobol quasi-random init → model-based MOO acquisition), so no hand-curated pilot designs are baked into the script. Ships a documented analytical `simulate_specimen` dummy evaluator (PETG mass model, topology stiffness, tiling factor, shore-softness cushion, infill strength scaling, infill-pattern stiffness, twist-angle sweet-spot bonus near 30°, build-orientation force multiplier, heteroscedastic noise) so the BO loop runs end-to-end without experimental data.
- **`requirements.txt`** — `honegumi==0.4.3`, `ax-platform==0.4.3`, `numpy<2`, `pandas<2.3`, `matplotlib`, `black>=24.0`. The `numpy<2` / `pandas<2.3` pins are required: ax 0.4.3 calls `np.percentile(..., interpolation=...)` (gone in numpy 2) and writes to DataFrame-backed arrays that pandas 3 returns read-only. `black` is pinned explicitly because `generate_scaffold.py` imports it to format the rendered scaffold.
- **`README.md`** — config table mapped to honegumi's curriculum tutorials, regen/run instructions, a "Customized campaign" section documenting the PR #24-aligned variables/objectives in `tensegrity_campaign.py`, and a checklist for swapping the dummy evaluator for the experimental data layer.
- **`tests/`** — pytest smoke tests covering the honegumi engine build, rendered-script structure, and full-vs-smoke iteration count of the scaffold generator. (The previous campaign-script smoke tests were removed once `tensegrity_campaign.py` became a flat top-level script — importing it would otherwise trigger the BO loop during test collection.)

### `CONFIG`
`Multi` objective · `Default` model · `Single` task · `categorical=True` · `custom_threshold=True` · `existing_data=True` · `synchrony=Batch` · `visualize=True`. Constraints (`sum`/`order`/`linear`/`composition`) off; flip in `CONFIG` and re-run the generator.

```bash
pip install -r bo/requirements.txt
python bo/generate_scaffold.py                       # (re)render bo/tensegrity_bo.py
python bo/generate_scaffold.py --smoke-test -o /tmp/smoke.py
MPLBACKEND=Agg python /tmp/smoke.py                  # fast end-to-end check
MPLBACKEND=Agg python bo/tensegrity_campaign.py      # customized campaign (edit N_ITERATIONS in-place for longer runs)
```

### Repo plumbing
- Top-level `README.md` gains a BO section + structure entry.
- `.gitignore` ignores `__pycache__/`, `*.py[cod]`, `.pytest_cache/`, `*.egg-info/`, and the generated `bo/campaign_pareto.png`.
- `bo/__init__.py` + `bo/tests/__init__.py` make `bo` a real package so tests don't manipulate `sys.path`.

### Verification
- `MPLBACKEND=Agg python bo/tensegrity_campaign.py` → 10 BO-selected trials (Sobol-initialized), 4 Pareto-optimal designs, Pareto-front PNG written.
- `pytest bo/tests` → generator scaffold smoke tests (3 tests; 2 pre-existing `black.report.NothingChanged` failures are unrelated to the PETG variable update).

### Notes for review
- Regeneration of `tensegrity_bo.py` is byte-stable; commit it alongside any `CONFIG` change rather than editing the generated file by hand. `tensegrity_bo.py` now also captures the `trial_index` returned by `attach_trial()` when seeding existing data (the previous loop-counter assumption was fragile if Ax trial indices ever diverged).

#### Seed candidates sent to Edison

**Project backronyms:** `BOOST` · `BLAST` · `IMPACT` · `ABSORB` · `DAMPEN` · `TIGER` · `SPRING` · `TUNE` · `TIBO` · `CUSHION`

#### Edison round-1 recommendation

**Top backronyms:**
1. **DAMPEN** — *Data-driven Architecture for Multi-material Printed Energy-absorbing Networks*. Strong mechanics verb, natural expansion, low–medium collision risk.
2. **TIBO** — *Tensegrity-Inspired Bayesian Optimization*. Short, distinctive, methodologically accurate; pair with a subtitle.
3. **BUMPER** — *Bayesian Uncertainty-guided Multi-material Printing for Energy Reduction*. Evokes the impact-absorber / crutch-tip application class.

**Avoid (high software-trademark collision per Edison):** BOOST (Boost C++ libraries), BLAST (bioinformatics tool, Altschul et al. 1990), SPRING (Spring Java framework), IMPACT (too generic).

### Added candidate: BOUNCE (per PR comment)

- **BOUNCE** — *Bayesian Optimization of Unit-cell Networks for Compression and Energy-absorption* ⭐
- **BOUNCE** — *Bayesian Optimization of Undergraduate-built Networks for Compression Experiments*
- **BOUNCE** — *Bayesian Optimization of Unit-cell Networks under Cyclic Excitation*

### Repo name decision

Per PR comment: **stay as `tensegrity-optimization`**. No rename / slug change is required. README/proposal title work is deferred until the project-name pick is made.

Follow-up `LITERATURE` task referencing the funding venues from issue #43 (NSF CMMI/DMREF/CAREER/EPSCoR, DOE EERE/ARPA-E, NIH NIBIB/NICHD, DOD ONR/AFOSR/ARO, NASA Space Tech, DARPA, DOT, NIST, SBIR/STTR, foundations) and grant-proposal-title professionalism constraints. - All trajectory artifacts the Edison client exposes are committed (`formatted_answer` + full structured `model_dump_json`):

- **Bounce® (P&G dryer-sheet trademark)** — branding overlap (mcgrath2000thebounceback!).
- **BOUNCE BACK! / Bounce Back resiliency curriculum** — a *program-name* collision in school-based mental-health programming, especially salient for NIH NICHD / NCMRR study sections (anthony2015promotingmentalhealth).

1. *Bayesian Optimization for Unit-cell Networks in **Crashworthiness** and Energy absorption* — swaps "Compression" → "Crashworthiness" (more engineering-property tone).
2. *Bayesian Optimization Under Noisy/Costly Experiments* — reframes around the multifidelity bottleneck; venue-agnostic.

Capitalization tip: keep it as **BOUNCE** (all-caps, never "Bounce") to dampen the consumer-brand association, and always pair with a colon-subtitle.

#### Per-venue ranking (Edison)

| Venue | 1st | 2nd | 3rd | 4th |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NSF CMMI / DMREF | TIBO | DAMPEN | BOUNCE | BUMPER |
| NIH NIBIB / NICHD | TIBO | DAMPEN | BUMPER | BOUNCE ⚠ (Bounce Back collision) |
| DOD ONR / AFOSR / ARO | TIBO | DAMPEN | BOUNCE | BUMPER |

The issue asks which base unit-cell structures and design variables should drive the Bayesian optimization campaign for **TPU + PETG** multi-material 3D-printed tensegrity-inspired energy absorbers — note PETG, not the PLA currently described in `proposal.tex`.

The repo is LaTeX-only (no BO code), so this is a research/scoping task. Following the established Edison-driven research pattern in this repo, a non-blocking literature query was submitted, the completed result is now committed under `edison-trajectories/`, and a follow-up synthesis cross-references the design-gap families surfaced by PR #22 and recasts the combined set of axes as an Ax `HierarchicalSearchSpace`.

### Changes
- **No source/proposal edits** — deferred until PETG-vs-PLA scope is confirmed.
- **Edison `LITERATURE_HIGH` task** — `task_id 5ae24eaf-5b6e-45cf-9f6c-1c7fbd881738` submitted, fetched (status: success), and committed:
  - `edison-trajectories/tpu-petg-bo-variables-5ae24eaf-5b6e-45cf-9f6c-1c7fbd881738.md` — verbatim `formatted_answer` (Question + cited Answer + numbered References).
  - `edison-trajectories/tpu-petg-bo-variables-5ae24eaf-5b6e-45cf-9f6c-1c7fbd881738.json` — full structured `model_dump_json` for reproducibility.
- **PR #22 design-gaps synthesis** — `edison-trajectories/tpu-petg-bo-variables-additions-from-pr22.md` cross-references the design-gap families from the PR #22 Edison survey (`6226a551-…`: Snelson X-module, Pajunen truncated-octa, Oster reentrant auxetic, Rhode-Barbarigos pentagonal ring, Pugh diamond / zig-zag, tensegrity torus, Hanaor double-layer grid, bistable double-prism, 6-bar wheel patent, etc.) against the original 5ae24eaf variable table and identifies the *additional* BO axes those families introduce:
  - 8 new categorical axes: extended `unit_cell` list, `chirality_pattern`, `cable_routing` (Pugh diamond/zig-zag/circuit), `tensegrity_class` (1/2/k), `tendon_clustering`, `bistable_mode`, `payload_carrier`, `tessellation_pattern`.
  - 5 new or conditional continuous axes: per-tendon prestress group fractions, `N_bay` stack count, re-entrancy angle (auxetic family), ring radius / strut-circuit count (ring & torus families), hub/cradle mass fraction.
  - Constraint: defer class-2 / class-k topologies until the issue #38 Phase-4 joint designs validate strut-to-strut contact; reaffirms TPU **85A** (not 95A) as the lab tendon material.
- **Hierarchical search space (§D of the additions doc)** — per [facebook/Ax#140](https://github.com/facebook/Ax/issues/140), the combined parameter set is recast as an Ax `HierarchicalSearchSpace`:
  - Root `topology_family` `ChoiceParameter` with 8 branches: `prism_stack`, `icosa_class`, `trunc_octa`, `ring_torus`, `auxetic_periodic`, `double_layer_grid`, `bistable_cell`, `x_module_weave`.
  - Per-branch `dependents={...}` map demoting `chirality_pattern`, `cable_routing`, `payload_carrier`/`hub_mass_fraction`, `tessellation_pattern`, `bistable_mode`, `tendon_clustering`, `re_entrancy_angle`, `ring_radius`/`N_circuit`, and the per-tendon prestress simplex from flat axes to conditional children of the relevant branch.
  - `joint_validated_class2` fixed feature on the Ax `Experiment` to gate the `ring_torus` / class-2 branch on issue #38 Phase-4 joint validation.
  - Surrogate / acquisition guidance: stratified Sobol seed (≥3 specimens per family) before BO turn-on, with a `MultiTaskGP` alternative (topology family as task feature) for the ~50–100-specimen budget.

### Query scope (original 5ae24eaf task)
- **(A) Base unit-cell topologies** — 3-/4-bar prisms, octahedron, icosahedron, expanded octahedron, truncated tetrahedron, Pajunen-style tensegrity-inspired cells, stacked-prism / lattice tilings; manufacturability and reported energy-absorption notes.
- **(B) Design variables** to expose to BO:
  - *Geometric/topological:* strut L, D, slenderness L/D, cable/skin cross-section, prestress, twist, tiling Nx·Ny·Nz, relative density, connectivity.
  - *Material/print:* PETG layer height, infill % & pattern; TPU shore (85A/95A), wall count, infill; nozzle/bed temps; speed; PETG–TPU wrap thickness (Ye 2023, Khatri 2024).
  - *Loading:* drop height, impactor mass, strain rate — fixed, not BO vars.
- **(C) PETG-vs-PLA implications** for sensible bounds (toughness, lower stiffness, lower Tg → strut slenderness, infill, layer-adhesion ranges).
- **(D) Recommended numeric bounds + categories** sized for a BoTorch/Ax search space and a ~50–100-specimen undergrad campaign.
- **(E) Primary objectives** (peak transmitted force, SEA, compaction efficiency, plateau stress) and constraints (mass, print time, cycle durability).

### Follow-up
- When the BO search space is first encoded, consume the original 5ae24eaf table plus the PR #22 synthesis additions using the §D hierarchical tree — concretely as Ax `ChoiceParameter(dependents=...)` Python or JSON — and apply the `joint_validated_class2` fixed feature for the class-2/k deferral constraint.
- If PETG is confirmed as the strut material, update `proposal.tex` parameterization wording (currently PLA+TPU) accordingly.

Stands up the journal-manuscript skeleton called for in the issue and populates it from existing repo context (proposal narrative, Edison literature trajectories across PR branches). Primary venue is ASME Journal of Mechanical Design (JMD); Smart Materials and Structures (SMS) is documented as a backup. Quantitative results remain `\todo{}` placeholders pending experimental data.

### `manuscript/` (new)
- `manuscript-body.tex` — shared IMRaD body using the `asmejour` class (CTAN; auto-installed by MiKTeX, not vendored). Uses the actual class macros (`\JourName`, `\SetAuthorBlock{...\CorrespondingAuthor}{...}`, `\title`, `\keywords`, `\maketitle`), `\DocumentMetadata` for PDF/A, JMD-formatted abstract, contributions list, three Background subsections (tensegrity, multi-material AM, BO), four Methods subsections (parameterization, fabrication, testing, BO loop), Results/Discussion stubs, Conclusions, and the JMD-required Acknowledgment (singular, per ASME) / Funding Data / Conflict of Interest blocks. Class options `[lineno,singlecolumn,nocopyright,upint,varvw,hyphenate]` give a single-column line-numbered draft; drop `singlecolumn`/`nocopyright` for the two-column ASME final.
- `manuscript.tex` — thin wrapper that sets `\def\TODOOPTS{disable}` and `\input{manuscript-body}` → clean reader-facing PDF (todonotes hidden).
- `manuscript-todos.tex` — thin wrapper that leaves `\TODOOPTS` empty → review PDF with margin annotations and `\listoftodos`.
- `references.bib` — **consolidated working bibliography** aggregating Edison-derived literature from across the repo's PR branches: proposal references, BO-algorithms PRECEDENT review (`copilot/write-draft-abstract`), NASA / aerospace literature (`copilot/create-latex-template-proposal`), tensegrity-impact extras (`copilot/increase-experimentation-mentoring`), and **27 new crutch-tip prior-art entries parsed from PR #18's `edison-trajectories/01-...md` and `02-...md`** (Segura 2007, Manocha 2021, Rasouli 2020, Brasil-Barros-da-Silva 2022, Dozono 2015, MacGillivray 2016, Zhang 2011, Mottaghi 2025, Stasiak-Cieślak 2025, Santos 2023, Yavas 2022, Arifvianto 2022, Ezeh 2018, Vanaei 2021, Ruwais 2025, plus footwear/insole lattice studies). The `pajunen2019` overlap was deduped. `\bibliographystyle{asmejour}` (numeric).
- `references-full.bib` — **master synthesized library** (see "Master synthesized bibliography" below); the working superset pool, not wired into the `pdflatex` build.
- `README.md` — JMD limits (Research ≤9 000 words, Tech Brief ~4 000, Design Innovation ~7 000), 150–200-word Latin-only abstract rule, IMRaD requirement, ASME numeric refs, links to the submission portal/companion site/CTAN package; SMS aside (no hard word limit, 200–300-word abstract, `iopart`); description of the two-builds todonotes toggle; documentation of `references-full.bib` and its regeneration command.
- `manuscript.pdf` (clean, 9 pp), `manuscript-todos.pdf` (review with margin notes + `\listoftodos`, 10 pp), and `manuscript-diff.pdf` (latexdiff, 9 pp) committed per repo convention.
- `preview/manuscript-versions.png` — side-by-side preview of page 1 (clean ↔ todos) for review; `preview/manuscript-real-figures.png` — preview of Fig 2 + Fig 3 with the harvested real photos.

### Placeholder system
- `todonotes` package wired through a single `\TODOOPTS` flag so both PDFs share `manuscript-body.tex` and the same numbered structure.
- `\figplaceholder{label}{caption}` and `\tabplaceholder{label}{caption}` macros render visible placeholder boxes at every figure/table location, vanishing automatically when `\TODOOPTS=disable`. (The figure slots have since been populated — see "Real-image figure population" below; the remaining `\tabplaceholder` is the repeatability table, pending data.)
- All known content gaps are flagged with `\todo{...}` so reviewers can audit them via `\listoftodos`.

### Build / repo plumbing
- `Makefile`: new `manuscript` (clean PDF), `manuscript-todos` (review PDF), `manuscript-all` (both), and `clean-manuscript` / `distclean-manuscript` targets that `cd manuscript && pdflatex/bibtex/pdflatex/pdflatex` against the appropriate wrapper. Existing `proposal` build is untouched.
- Top-level `README.md`: pointer to the new scaffold.
- `.gitignore`: ignore `manuscript-orig.tex` (latexdiff source artifact, matching the existing `proposal-orig.tex` entry), `manuscript/*.tdo` todonotes build artefacts, Python bytecode (`__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`), and the Edison upload bundles/zips (`edison-trajectories/review-followups/fabfig-bundle*`, `edison-trajectories/mechfig-feedback/bundle*`, `edison-trajectories/mock-jmd-review-2/*bundle*`).

### Edison mock peer review (ANALYSIS task `6c140449-0426-490d-8fc2-67bcfdd0d1d9`)
- Submitted the populated draft (PDFs, all three `.tex` files, `references.bib`, `manuscript/README.md`) to Edison ANALYSIS with a prompt requesting three characteristic mock reviewers (Design / Mech Eng, Biomechanics / Rehab, AM / Materials) plus a mock JMD Associate Editor decision letter and a "bibliographic gaps" section.
- Verbatim trajectory committed under `edison-trajectories/2026-05-09-mock-jmd-review-6c140449.md` (formatted answer + query) and `.json` (full structured `task.model_dump_json()` for reproducibility), following the repo's Edison-trajectory convention.
- Triaged analysis at `reviews/mock-jmd-review-analysis.md` mapping reviewer feedback to specific files/sections with a priority-ordered fix list. Mock decision: **Reject and Resubmit**; venue fit confirmed for ASME JMD as a Research Paper (alternatives flagged: SMS, *Additive Manufacturing*).

### First-pass blocker fixes (per PR comment)
- **`(author?)` bibtex artefacts fixed.** Root cause was `\citet{...}` resolving against the `asmejour.bst` output, which emits raw author text without natbib's `\bibinfo{author}` annotation. All eight `\citet{...}` calls in `manuscript-body.tex` were rewritten to inline-author form (e.g. `Pajunen et~al.~\cite{...}`). Two pre-existing unescaped `&` in `references.bib` `journal` fields (`requejo2005upperextremitykinetics`, `macgillivray2016theinfluenceof`) were also fixed (`& physics` → `\& physics`). Verified via `pdftotext manuscript.pdf | grep '(author?)'` → 0 hits.
- **Blank third Contributions bullet filled.** Replaced the bare `\todo{}` `\item` with a substantive third contribution describing a planned two-fidelity escalation path (pretensioned tensegrity assemblies with true cables and measured pretension, per Sterling's "somewhat TBD" note); the surrogate / fusion-strategy choice (co-Kriging vs. nonlinear information-fusion priors) is left as an explicit `\todo{}`.
- **Bibliographic gaps from the AE letter added.** New bib entries + inline citations for ISO 11334-4 (`iso11334-4`, walking-aid test methods, Methods §3.3); Caminero et~al. 2019 (`caminero2019printingparameters`, FFF interface adhesion, Background §2.2); Garrido-Merchán & Hernández-Lobato 2020 (`garridomerchan2020dealingwithcategorical`) and Baptista & Poloczek 2018 BOCS (`baptista2018bocs`) for categorical-variable BO (Background §2.3 + Methods §3.4). The FFF resolution-limits reference was *not* added — left as a `\todo{}` placeholder pending a vetted citation, per Sterling's "don't guess" instruction.
- **PLA → PETG global rewrite** deferred to issue #45 per PR comment.
- **Methodological gaps** (BO rigor / kernel / categorical-encoding details, FFF process-parameter table, SEA→peak-transmitted-force mapping, cyclic/off-axis loading) **kept as `\todo{}` placeholders** per Sterling's "don't guess" instruction.

### Cross-PR planned-methods refresh (per PR comment)
Walked every open PR and recent branch and folded the concrete planned-methods progress into `manuscript-body.tex`. Results/Discussion remain `\todo{}` placeholders by design — the project is at the planned-methods phase. Citation slots for unreleased Edison briefs were left as `\todo{}` rather than guessing bib keys.

- **Intro** — explicit "manuscript status" callout: planned-methods phase, Results/Discussion intentionally placeholders.
- **Background §2.1** — Davami 2025 dynamic AM tensegrity + Intrigila 2022 closest analog (PR #58).
- **Methods §3.1 Design Parameterization** — names the $T_3$-prism working prototype ($\sim$50 mm bounding box), cable-diameter categorical $\{1.2,1.8,2.4,3.0,4.5\}$ mm, and the $D_3$-orbit-axis reduction from 12 → 4 member-diameter axes (PR #24 heterogeneous-params brief, PR #35 CAD).
- **Methods §3.2 Multi-Material Fabrication** — Bambu Lab H2D dual-nozzle platform; dovetail (Design B) primary + anchor-bulb (Design A) backup joints with captive TPU core inside PLA shell (PR #39 Phase-3/4 joint design); manual narrowing-pillar TPU-safe support workflow + 10° threshold Bambu Studio recipe (PR #66) + H2D multi-part assignment fix reference (PR #64).
- **Methods §3.3 Experimental Characterization** — Instron quasi-static protocol per ASTM D638/D412/E111/F2971 + ISO/ASTM 52900/52921 with the 5 kN → 100–500 N load-cell swap (PR #49/#50); bungee-assisted Hill drop tower with top-tether/specimen-base-registration mitigations (PR #67 + Jeff's note); planned Lansmont M23 + Polytec QTec higher-fidelity replicate campaign (PR #28); five per-modality objective-function briefs + cross-modality ANALYSIS synthesis (PR #60).
- **Methods §3.4 BO Loop** — Ax `HierarchicalSearchSpace` scaffolding (PR #30); $n=9$ Sobol initialization batch in $3\times3$ plate layout (PR #35); SAASBO + qNEHVI default acquisition pairing with TuRBO escalation only above $\sim$25 D (PR #24 follow-up).

### Master synthesized bibliography (per PR comment)
Synthesized a single master library from **every branch and every Edison query** in the repo into `manuscript/references-full.bib` — **813 unique references** (592 with DOIs, 213 with abstracts), drawn from **38 distinct Edison tasks plus the committed project bibs**. This is a working superset pool and is intentionally *not* wired into the `pdflatex` build, which still cites the curated `manuscript/references.bib` to keep the printed bibliography focused.

- **`scripts/edison/build_master_bib.py` (new)** — reproducible extractor. Unshallows the clone and pulls all 34+ branches, content-deduplicates every `edison-trajectories/**/*.json` and every committed project `.bib` (excluding the `sterling-cv/` personal-publication lists), and parses references from both representations the Edison jobs emit: rich inline `BibTex:` blocks (author/title/journal/doi + a following `Abstract:` block) and, as a fallback for tasks whose raw evidence blocks weren't retained, the numbered `References` list in `formatted_answer` so no cited key is dropped. The citation key (`<surname><year><titlewords>`) is used to split author/title/venue robustly even for ALL-CAPS or non-Latin author names. Entries are deduplicated by key then DOI (richest record wins), with the union of source task IDs recorded in a leading `% source:` comment per entry for traceability; HTML entities are decoded and `&` is BibTeX-escaped to `\&`.
- **Edison API for missing artifacts** — the `*-SUBMITTED.json` placeholders were polled via the Edison API; most are `ANALYSIS` jobs with no bibliography, but `PHASE4-context` (`f9804247…`) was a completed `LITERATURE_HIGH` task, so it was re-fetched (`get_task(...).model_dump_json()`) and folded in (+3 unique references). Separate-account tasks that the API can't return would need manual lookup; none were required to reach the current set.
- **Validation** — brace-balanced, no empty fields, every entry has a title, and `&`/HTML entities are escaped.
- `manuscript/README.md` documents `references-full.bib`, the `% source:` provenance scheme, and the regeneration command.

### One-by-one DOI verification / abstract enrichment (per PR comment)
Went through the master library DOI-by-DOI to confirm each DOI actually points at the cited paper, enrich abstracts, and find missing DOIs — driven by a reproducible tool that checks each DOI against its **authoritative registered metadata** rather than guessing.

- **`scripts/edison/verify_bib_dois.py` (new)** — fetches each DOI's CSL JSON via doi.org content negotiation + Crossref, compares the registered title to the cited title (jaccard / `SequenceMatcher` similarity plus containment coverage), and conservatively applies only hand-verified edits. LaTeX-escaped DOIs (`\_`, `\&`, etc.) are unescaped before querying so they don't spuriously 404. The Crossref polite-pool contact is configurable via the `CROSSREF_MAILTO` env var. Contains hand-verified decision tables (`DOI_FIX`, `NODOX_FIX`, `CONFIRM_ABSTRACT`, `SUSPECT`).
- **Result over `manuscript/references-full.bib`:** all 592 DOIs checked against their registered titles; **+179 abstracts** added from each entry's own DOI record (JATS/HTML stripped, `&` escaped) → 213 → **393 abstracts**; **1 wrong DOI fixed** (`zhang2015tensegrity`, which pointed at an unrelated squash-mode-vibration paper, corrected to `10.1063/1.5040850` — the real *Tensegrity cell mechanical metamaterial*, APL 2018 — with abstract + year); **+12 missing DOIs** found via Crossref and confirmed by author+title → 592 → **604 DOIs**. bibtexparser confirmed the edit was lossless (no original fields dropped/changed beyond the intended ones).
- **Flagged wrong / unresolvable DOIs:** six entries whose DOIs resolve to an unrelated paper or 404 with no confident replacement (`fraternali2015tensegrity` → ceramics, `witze2023osirisrex` → rural health, `wang2022bayesian` → polyelectrolyte gel, `lee2023bayesian` 404, `grosu2025methodsforassessing` 404, `wang2024simbencharulebased` title mismatch).
- **Edison query for the remainder** — the six suspect DOIs plus the ~210 entries still lacking a DOI were written to `edison-trajectories/bib-doi-verification/needs-list.md` and submitted as Edison `LITERATURE_HIGH` task `dbd490f6-edbc-4b8e-8778-b41e166b42ca` (via `scripts/edison/submit_bib_doi_verification.py`) asking for correct DOIs and link verification. The task is async; its results are to be fetched in a future session and folded back into the bib. The submission and its provenance are recorded in `edison-trajectories/bib-doi-verification/` (`README.md`, `needs-list.md`, `bib-doi-verification-SUBMITTED.json`).
- 237 DOI'd entries still carry no abstract because Crossref does not expose one for those records — expected, not a defect. `manuscript/README.md` documents this verification/enrichment pass.

### Reviewer-feedback corrections (per @me-madsen review)
Folded @me-madsen's inline review of `manuscript-body.tex` into the draft and rebuilt all three PDFs:

- **TPU joint mechanism corrected.** The draft incorrectly described the TPU tension elements as being wrapped around the strut exterior via Ye et al.'s core-encapsulation / "core-wrapping" strategy. Per the reviewer, the actual method anchors the TPU *inside* the ends of each PLA strut — the cables meeting at a given strut end join within the strut, which acts as a rigid cage, then exit through discrete outlets. Updated in the Contributions list, Methods §3.2, and the Conclusions. Rather than assert that this internal-anchoring junction is validated by Ye et al., a `\todo{}` now flags that the analogy must be verified (against PR #39 / PR #35) before it is claimed.
- **"IDEX" removed** from the Bambu Lab H2D printer description, since the H2D is a dual-nozzle (not Independent Dual Extruder) printer.
- **BOCS baseline reworded** from the awkward "the BOCS combinatorial baseline of [ref]" to "the BOCS combinatorial baseline [ref]"; the concrete baseline metric remains a `\todo{}`.
- **SAASBO and TuRBO acronyms expanded** at first use ("sparse axis-aligned subspace BO (SAASBO)", "trust-region BO (TuRBO)"); qNEHVI is already spelled out at its first use earlier in the BO section.

### Mechanism-oriented data figure example (side-task, per PR comment 4664748222)
Per @sgbaird's request, a standalone *example* of a mechanism-oriented data figure — processed drop-test deceleration curves with callouts to the specific structural features being tested. At the time it was a self-contained mock-up; it has **since been wired into the manuscript** as the §3.3 `fig:dropcurve` illustrative example (see "Real-image figure population" below).

- **`scripts/figures/mechanistic_data_figure_example.py` (new)** — matplotlib generator producing **synthetic** (clearly watermarked) but physically plausible curves anchored to the documented issue-#36 drop-test behaviour (125 kHz TP4/PicoScope-class capture, SAE J211 CFC-180 filtering, impact ≈4.2 ms, control CFC-180 peak ≈1792 G, tensegrity ≈370–463 G ⇒ ~74–79 % reduction). No experimental file is read; the script is meant to have real processed channels + camera frames swapped in later.
- **Figure contents** — (a) processed response (rigid control vs. tensegrity, CFC-180 filtered, raw 125 kHz trace faded in to motivate filtering, peak-reduction callout, shaded mechanistic phases A contact/pre-tension, B strut+cable load-redistribution energy plateau, C rebound); (b) T3-prism specimen callout (red PLA struts in compression, blue TPU cables in tension); (c) internal-anchor joint callout (cables joining inside the strut-end cage); (d) phase-B deformation snapshot. In a real figure, panels (b)–(d) would be high-speed-camera frames / specimen photos registered to points on the curve.
- **`figures/examples/mechanistic-data-figure-example.{png,pdf}`** — rendered example, embedded in the PR reply.
- **`figures/examples/README.md`** — documents the figure as an illustrative mock-up (synthetic data) with the regeneration command.

### Edison feedback on the mechanistic data figure (side-task, per PR comment 4664873230)
Per @sgbaird's follow-up ("send this to edison analysis for feedback"), the mechanistic data-figure example was submitted to Edison **ANALYSIS** and the result folded back in. The example figure and the manuscript were left unchanged in this round — feedback only.

- **`scripts/edison/submit_mechfig_feedback.py` (new)** — bundles the figure (`png`/`pdf`), its generator, and README into a single zipped collection (required for ANALYSIS uploads) and submits ANALYSIS task `e0c4e062-15c7-4a62-b931-1746211fe8b1` asking for prioritized, actionable critique (mechanism storytelling, highest-value additional panels, camera-frame registration, synthetic-vs-real honesty / uncertainty reporting, layout/color/accessibility, and physics red flags).
- **`scripts/edison/fetch_mechfig_feedback.py` (new)** — polls the task to terminal state and writes the verbatim trajectory.
- **`edison-trajectories/mechfig-feedback/` (new)** — `README.md`, the `*-SUBMITTED.json` placeholder, and the fetched `mechfig-feedback-e0c4e062….{md,json}` trajectory; the upload bundle/zip are gitignored per the existing fabfig precedent.
- **Key findings:** the figure proves the performance contrast more clearly than the mechanism. Top asks are to add 3 synchronized curve markers + matching high-speed/DIC frames and a transmitted-force / cumulative-impulse subpanel, rename the generic A/B/C phases to event-based labels, and report replicate/uncertainty and filtering details in the caption. Edison also caught a physics bug in the synthetic generator — the control and tensegrity traces are not impulse-consistent (~8.9 vs ~23.9 m/s mass-normalized, ~2.7× too large) — plus a too-early tensegrity peak, an over-extreme duration contrast, and a Gaussian-shaped (rather than delayed-rise/flat-shoulder) plateau. **These were implemented in the revision below.**

### Mechanistic data figure — Edison feedback implemented (side-task, per PR comment 4673512526)
Per @sgbaird's request to implement the Edison ANALYSIS changes (PR comment 4664958219), the recorded feedback above was folded into `scripts/figures/mechanistic_data_figure_example.py` and the `figures/examples/mechanistic-data-figure-example.{png,pdf}` were regenerated.

- **Physics fixes (the bug Edison caught).** The control and tensegrity traces are now **impulse-consistent**: the control is anchored to the documented ~1792 G CFC-180 peak, and the tensegrity shoulder is scaled to the *same* mass-normalized Δv, so both integrate to ≈10.1 m/s. The tensegrity peak (~403 G ⇒ ~78 % reduction, within the documented 370–463 G / 74–79 % range) and the matched Δv are now *outputs* of impulse conservation rather than arbitrary inputs. The "plateau" is now a **delayed rise + flat shoulder** (smootherstep edges) that peaks *after* the control (~6.4 ms vs ~4.6 ms) instead of a too-early centered Gaussian, with a realistic (not ~10×) duration contrast.
- **Layout / storytelling.** Added a **cumulative-impulse subpanel (a2)** sharing panel (a)'s x-axis showing both traces converging to the matched Δv; **3 synchronized numbered markers** (contact → plateau → rebound) on the tensegrity curve that key **frame placeholders (b)–(d)**, each stamped with its time; **event-based phase labels** (first contact / strut rotation + cable redistribution / peak compression plateau / rebound) with the key kept off the data field; **n=5 replicate ±1 s.d. bands** with filtering disclosure (125 kHz raw, SAE J211 CFC-180, zero-phase filtfilt, CH4 first-contact alignment) moved into the caption; and a **colorblind-safer pair** (dark gray control / blue-green tensegrity), lighter phase shading, and a fainter watermark.
- The generator optionally uses SciPy for cumulative integration (NumPy-trapezoid fallback if SciPy is absent) and remains NumPy-2-compatible. `figures/examples/README.md` was updated to describe the revised panels and the impulse-conservation framing.

### Ax-generated example fills for the empty figure slots (side-task, per PR comment 4673509625)
Per @sgbaird's request ("create actual placeholder figures for any of the figures that are actually just empty slots, e.g. an example of LOO-CV plots obtained from Ax using dummy data"), produced drop-in example fills for the four data-figure slots in `manuscript-body.tex` (`fig:loocv`, `fig:sensitivity`, `fig:convergence`, `fig:pareto`). These are self-contained, watermarked illustrative examples and have **since been wired into the manuscript** (see "Real-image figure population" below).

- **`scripts/figures/ax_placeholder_figures_example.py` (new)** — runs a **real Ax Bayesian-optimization loop** (`ax.api.Client`: Sobol initialization + BoTorch model-based trials — the SAASBO/qNEHVI machinery the manuscript describes) over a tensegrity-flavoured search space (strut diameter, twist, pretension, categorical cable diameter $\in\{1.2,1.8,2.4,3.0,4.5\}$ mm), evaluated by a synthetic surrogate, then renders each diagnostic the real campaign would produce. Only the **objective values are synthetic** (a closed-form `evaluate()`), so the diagnostics are genuine Ax/BoTorch output; the access to the fitted adapter (`client._generation_strategy.adapter`, no public accessor in Ax 1.3.1) is centralized in one documented helper.
- **Figures (`figures/examples/`, each `.png`+`.pdf`)** — `ax-loocv-example` (leave-one-out cross-validation of the GP surrogate via `ax.adapter.cross_validation.cross_validate`, predicted vs. observed SEA & peak force with model error bars and $R^2_{\rm LOO}$); `ax-sensitivity-example` (parameter-sensitivity ranking from model length-scale importances per objective); `ax-convergence-example` (best-so-far SEA vs. number of experiments, BO vs. an **independent** uniform random-search baseline, shaded $n=9$ Sobol-init region); `ax-pareto-example` (Pareto front in (peak transmitted force, SEA) space with all evaluated designs). `ax-placeholder-figures-contact-sheet.png` is a 2×2 preview embedded in the PR reply.
- **`figures/examples/README.md`** — documents the four fills, their slot mapping, the synthetic-objectives caveat, and the regeneration command (requires `ax-platform`, which pulls in `botorch`/`torch`).

### Real-image figure population (per PR comment 4677526117)
Per @sgbaird's request to wire the Ax (comment 4673681822) and mechanistic (comment 4673786958) example figures into the manuscript and to fill Fig 2 / Fig 3 with **real images extracted from the repo's issue & PR comment history** (using the GitHub API on the full comment JSON):

- **Example figures wired into `manuscript-body.tex`.** The mechanistic drop-test figure is now §3.3 `fig:dropcurve` (Fig 4); the four Ax diagnostics fill the formerly-empty `\figplaceholder` slots `fig:loocv`/`fig:sensitivity`/`fig:convergence`/`fig:pareto` (Figs 5–8). All five are honestly captioned **"Illustrative example (synthetic data)"** and keep their watermarks, with in-text references added for each. The redundant BO-loop schematic was replaced by the surrogate diagnostics.
- **Fig 2 (`fig:printed-prototypes`) populated** with a parametric CAD render (a) beside a real as-printed T3-prism photo (b) carrying TikZ callouts for the strut diameter $d_s$, tendon diameter $d_t$, and cell height $H$. Fixed an `asmejour` gotcha in the process: its `subfigure` environment auto-emits the `(a)/(b)` sublabels and forbids an inner `\caption` — using one spawns phantom figures and corrupts the main figure numbering; rewrote the block to use the class's native `subfigure` correctly.
- **Fig 3 (`fig:fab-workflow`) populated** — the fabrication/characterization workflow TikZ nodes now embed real photos (OpenSCAD render, Bambu Studio dual-nozzle slice, H2D mid-print, post-processed specimen, drop-tower fixture) instead of text-only boxes; removed the "populate nodes" `\todo`.
- **`figures/photos/` (new)** — six harvested, cropped, and EXIF-orientation-corrected photographs plus a `README.md` provenance table mapping each to its source comment and manuscript usage.
- **`scripts/figures/fetch_repo_photos.py` (new)** — reproducible extractor that re-downloads the exact source attachments (handling `user-attachments` S3 redirects via `curl` and rewriting `github.com/.../blob/...?raw=true` links to `raw.githubusercontent.com`) and re-applies the recorded crops; 5/6 photos reproduce byte-identically, the sixth visually identically.
- **Consistency / docs.** `figures/examples/README.md` updated (no longer "not wired in"); rebuilt all three PDFs — `manuscript.pdf` (9 pp), `manuscript-todos.pdf` (10 pp), and `manuscript-diff.pdf` (9 pp). Added `preview/manuscript-real-figures.png`. The only remaining figure-area placeholder is the `\tabplaceholder{repeatability}` table, pending data.

### Pretensioning correction (per @sgbaird-alt review)
Per @sgbaird-alt's note that there should be no pretensioning in Figure 2 (the only pretensioning belongs in the scale-up validation of the final Pareto front), removed the "and pre-tension geometry imposed during printing" phrase from the TPU tension-elements design-variable description in Methods §3.1. The current BO-loop specimens and the Fig 2 prototype are now described as unpretensioned; pretensioning remains only in Contributions item 3 as a future high-fidelity validation step on the Pareto-optimal designs. Rebuilt `manuscript.pdf` (7 pp, two-column layout), `manuscript-todos.pdf` (10 pp), and `manuscript-diff.pdf` (9 pp, showing the deletion markup) from source so the committed PDFs reflect the fix.

### Second-round Edison mock peer review (per PR comment 4686431615)
Per @sgbaird's request ("send to Edison analysis for another round of mock reviewer feedback and report back the results … Commit all Edison artifacts"), the revised draft was submitted to Edison **ANALYSIS** for a second pass of the same three-reviewer + Associate-Editor panel.

- **`scripts/edison/submit_mock_jmd_review2.py` (new)** — bundles the rebuilt PDFs + all three `.tex` wrappers + `manuscript-body.tex` + `references.bib` + `manuscript/README.md` into a single zipped collection (required for ANALYSIS uploads) and submits ANALYSIS task `3fde560e-1bb9-4c6b-8fcc-eaeef4570bf4`, with a prompt summarizing what changed since round 1 so the panel focuses on the current state. Writes a `*-SUBMITTED.json` placeholder (including the verbatim query) for a later fetch.
- **`scripts/edison/fetch_mock_jmd_review2.py` (new)** — polls the task to terminal state and writes the verbatim trajectory (`.md` answer + query, `.json` full `model_dump_json`).
- **`edison-trajectories/mock-jmd-review-2/` (new)** — `README.md`, the `*-SUBMITTED.json` placeholder, and the fetched `mock-jmd-review-2-3fde560e….{md,json}` trajectory; the upload bundle/zip are gitignored per the existing precedent.
- **Key result:** the mock decision **improved from round 1's *Reject and Resubmit* to *Major Revision***. All three reviewers + the AE confirm the round-1 blockers are resolved (PLA/TPU consistency, internal-anchor joint description, a more concrete Ax/BoTorch BO section, honestly labeled synthetic figures, and the pretensioning correction). Top remaining asks — most still gated on the by-design-absent experimental results — are: populate Results/Discussion; resolve the general-energy-absorber vs. crutch-tip scope framing up front; reconcile Table 1 with the D3 four-orbit-axis claim and the categorical {1.2,1.8,2.4,3.0,4.5} mm vs. continuous 3.0–5.5 mm tendon-diameter conflict; fully specify the BO method (kernel, encoding, budget, stopping rule); add a novelty-comparison table vs. Pajunen 2019 / Intrigila 2022 / Mo 2023; soften "ensure cyclic interface durability" until data exist; standardize FDM/FFF; and expand the abstract toward the 150–200-word target. JMD venue fit reaffirmed (with *Additive Manufacturing* / *J. Mech. Behav. Biomed. Mater.* as alternatives). Feedback only this round — no manuscript edits beyond the pretensioning fix above, per the "don't guess" convention.

### Notes for review
- If retargeting to SMS, swap the class line to `\documentclass[12pt]{iopart}` and the bibstyle to `iopart-num`; `manuscript/README.md` flags this.
- Two `asmejour`-specific gotchas were uncovered while populating: the class redefines `enumerate`/`itemize` and rejects `enumitem`-style options (no `[leftmargin=*]`), and the `asmejour.bst` bibstyle requires BibTeX-canonical `" and "` author separators (Edison-trajectory comma-separated lists were converted automatically).
- A third gotcha surfaced during the blocker pass: `asmejour.bst` does **not** wrap author fields in natbib's `\bibinfo{author}{...}` macro, so `\citet{...}` always renders as `(author?) [n]`. Use `\cite{...}` with an inline author surname instead. `references.bib` `journal` fields containing `&` must be escaped as `\&`.
- A fourth gotcha (figure population): `asmejour`'s built-in `subfigure` environment auto-generates the `(a)/(b)` sublabels and forbids an inner `\caption`/`\subcaption`; an inner `\caption` increments the main figure counter and creates phantom figures, so subpanels must use `\begin{subfigure}[b]{width} ... \label{} \end{subfigure}` with all descriptive text in the single outer `\caption`.
- MiKTeX needs `pdfmanagement` and `xkeyval` pre-installed before `pdflatex --enable-installer -interaction=nonstopmode` will succeed end-to-end. On a TeXLive sandbox the `asmejour` class title additionally needs the TeX Gyre Heros Condensed fonts (`tex-gyre`) installed and registered via `updmap`, or the build fails with `ec-qhvcr not loadable`. The `asmejour` class/bst itself is fetched from CTAN (`macros/latex/contrib/asmejour.zip`) and the `.bst` installed into the `bibtex/bst/` texmf tree; `latexdiff` (TeX Live `texlive-extra-utils`) is needed for the diff PDF.

Per the issue, sent a single high-effort Edison `LITERATURE` query connecting the multi-material 3D-printed tensegrity / BO-driven energy-absorption framework to NASA / aerospace priorities, scoped to support the BYU NASA Space Grant proposal (#13, #14) and a NASA-aligned MRG revision. Results have been fetched and committed.

### Submission
- Job: `JobNames.LITERATURE`
- Task ID: `97002b89-5bad-4112-a1e0-7b924a2b66c1` (non-blocking submission)
- Final status: `success`

### Query structure (10 citation-dense sections, DOIs / NTRS IDs requested)
- NASA strategic roadmaps citing tensegrity / deployable / energy-absorbing structures (STMD, NIAC, ECF/ESI, Moon-to-Mars, Artemis, CLPS, MSR/EDL, OSAM, ISM)
- NASA-funded tensegrity work (Ames Super Ball Bot / TT-3, SunSpiral, Agogino, Iscen) and post-2020 follow-ons
- Landing-load attenuation vs. incumbent honeycomb / foam / airbag (MER, Mars 2020, Orion) with quantitative metrics (SEA, crush efficiency, plateau stress, peak/mean force)
- In-space & lunar additive manufacturing of multi-material FDM (ISS Made In Space / Redwire AMF, Refabricator)
- Space-environment behavior of PLA/TPU (thermal cycling, ASTM E595 outgassing, AO, UV, radiation)
- Deployable / morphing structures (booms, sails, habitats, BEAM/LIFE, origami) intersecting tensegrity
- MMOD / hypervelocity protection — lattice and Whipple-shield enhancements
- Bayesian optimization / active learning for aerospace lattice and impact-absorber design
- Mentored-undergraduate alignment with NASA workforce pipelines (Space Grant, Artemis Generation, EPSCoR, MUREP)
- 5–10 concrete NASA mission framings (lander crush cores, CubeSat shock isolators, sample-return attenuators, habitat liners, EVA crash structures, rover suspension, penetrators)

For each section the query requests 5–15 primary citations, a 1–2 paragraph synthesis, explicit gaps the proposed framework can fill, and target NASA solicitations.

### Repository changes
- Added `edison-responses/2026-05-08-nasa-priorities-literature-97002b89.md` containing the fetched `formatted_answer` (~66k chars) prepended with a header (task ID, job, submission/fetch dates, status, related issues #12/#13/#14).

The committed response will be incorporated into the Space Grant proposal scaffold (#14) and a NASA-aligned MRG revision in a follow-up PR.

body:
A 5-page proposal narrative for Marcus Madsen's Utah NASA Space Grant Consortium Fellowship application (advisor: Sterling Baird), written in Marcus's first-person voice. Scope mirrors the existing MRG (multi-material 3D-printed tensegrity-inspired energy absorbers + experimental Bayesian optimization) but is refocused end-to-end on NASA-relevant load cases and tightened to a single-student, single-fellowship-year campaign on the Bambu Lab H2D printer.

### Layout
- New `nasa-space-grant/` subdirectory keeps the fellowship proposal isolated from the existing MRG proposal at the repo root.
- `nasa-26.pdf` (root) — official application form/instructions, fetched from the BYU engineering site.

### Narrative (`nasa-space-grant/proposal.tex`)
- First-person voice from Marcus as the undergraduate applicant, with a final pass to remove third-person/about-Marcus phrasings ("undergraduate-friendly throughput" → "practical for me to run as a single-student campaign"; "an undergraduate, with a single multi-material FDM printer" → "a single student, with one multi-material FDM printer"; "year of focused undergraduate research" → "year of focused research"). Subsequent passes also retired collective phrasings — "our group has access to … practical for me to run as a single-student campaign" → "my lab has access to … practical for a single-student campaign"; "in our lab" → "in the Baird lab".
- Reframed around two NASA-relevant load cases: planetary lander crush cores and CubeSat / small-payload shock isolation (per NASA GSFC GEVS).
- Heavy use of the **Bambu Lab H2D** dual-nozzle multi-material FDM printer is called out throughout — PLA struts + TPU tension elements, ~50–100 specimens/year throughput.
- Sections: Introduction & Motivation, Background & Relation to NASA Priorities, Research Objectives, Proposed Approach & Methods (with quarterly task table), Expected Outcomes & Broader Impact, Qualifications & Mentoring Plan.

body:
Reorganizes the tensegrity MRG proposal from a generic academic structure into the MRG format (≤5 body pages + cover page, references, bio sketches). Updates technical content to reflect the multi-material 3D printing approach (PLA/TPU) and multifidelity BO framework, with undergraduate mentoring demonstrated implicitly throughout per official MRG guidelines. Incorporates Edison Scientific literature review and revision plan feedback to strengthen technical framing, add key references, and address feasibility concerns.

### New files
- **`sections/coverpage.tex`** — PI/Co-PI (Hill/Baird), ≤150-word abstract, budget summary table (MRG categories), relationship to external funding (self-contained framing)
- **`sections/biosketch.tex`** — Hill and Baird bio sketches in NSF format (placeholder publications per open questions in issue)
- **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`** — Pulled from main; Edison Scientific integration and Copilot agent conventions
- **`proposal-diff.tex` / `proposal-diff.pdf`** — Latexdiff output showing changes from prior version

### Proposal restructure (`proposal.tex`)
- Replaced old sections (Project Summary → Research Objectives → Technical Approach → Broader Impacts → Qualifications) with MRG structure: Research Motivation & Overview → Background → Student Project 1 (Simulation & BO) → Student Project 2 (Fabrication & Testing) → Mentoring Environment → Expected Outcomes → Potential Impact
- Individually scoped student projects with named deliverables and **mentoring outcomes** (skills development, conference presentations, co-authorship)
- Filled PI/Co-PI names, removed TODO placeholders from body
- Added **placeholder for overview figure** (Figure 1: tensegrity design → multi-material printing → BO loop) with TODO for replacement before submission

### Edison Scientific-informed revisions
- Used Edison Scientific (`edison-client`) LITERATURE query to generate a comprehensive technical mock review of the proposal
- Retrieved completed Edison Scientific **revision plan trajectory** (previously timed out) with prioritized action items
- **Reframed as "tensegrity-inspired"** throughout proposal and cover page — Edison flagged that TPU tension elements behave as viscoelastic solids, not ideal cables, so "tensegrity-inspired" is more defensible than strict "tensegrity"
- **TPU damping framed as asset**: Rate-dependent damping behavior explicitly noted as an advantage for energy absorption, not merely a deviation from ideal cable behavior
- **Added 3 new references** identified by Edison review:
  - Pajunen et al. 2019 (*Materials & Design*): 3D-printable tensegrity-inspired structures with drop-weight impact validation
  - Ye et al. 2023 (*Nature Communications*): Multimaterial PLA/TPU wrapping strategy for robust rigid–soft interfaces
  - Khatri & Egan 2024 (*3D Printing and Additive Manufacturing*): ABS/TPU multimaterial honeycomb energy absorption
- **Adopted Ye et al. core-wrapping strategy** language for PLA–TPU interface durability (rigid PLA struts encapsulated by continuous TPU skins) throughout Student Project 2 and Background
- **Added Go/No-Go LF–HF validation gate**: Explicit correlation check (R² < 0.8 on simulated vs. measured energy absorption → pivot to single-fidelity experimental BO) in Student Project 1, Background, and timeline
- **De-scoped wave propagation metrics**: Replaced with tangible, operationally measurable **specific energy absorption (SEA)** and **compaction efficiency** metrics per Edison Priority 4 recommendation
- **Framed risk mitigation as student learning modules** in Student Development Outcomes (interface characterization, Go/No-Go data interpretation, wrapping strategies)
- Added **interface testing** and **LF–HF correlation gate** milestones to project timeline

### Mentoring-first focus
- Mentoring demonstrated implicitly throughout proposal structure and content rather than stated as an explicit objective — mentoring environment section opens with the student development pathway ("guided exploration to independent research ownership")
- **Relationship to External Funding** rewritten as self-contained MRG (not seed funding for NSF)
- **Expected Research Outcomes** leads with "Trained undergraduate researchers" rather than publications
- Student project sections use "Mentoring outcomes" framing instead of "Expected outcomes"
- Timeline replaces "NSF proposal preparation" with "Peer mentoring of new students"
- Expanded **Mentoring Environment** section with layered mentoring model, skill-building workshops (scientific writing, presentation skills, research ethics), progressive responsibility culminating in project ownership, and sustainable researcher pipeline
- Restructured Skills Development into **Student Development Outcomes** organized by category (Technical, Communication, Professional)
- Removed explicit diversity recruiting statement per reviewer feedback

### Content updates
- Multi-material 3D printing: TPU tension + PLA struts on single platform
- Added Mo et al. (2023) as key reference; framed multifidelity BO around it (simulations = low-fidelity, experiments = high-fidelity)
- Named conferences: ASME IDETC, UCUR; named journals: ASME J. Mech. Design, Smart Mater. & Struct.
- Added industry motivation: protective equipment, packaging, aerospace

### Writing style improvements
- **Converted bullet-heavy sections to flowing prose**: Student Project 1 and 2 deliverables (from `enumerate` to narrative paragraphs), Mentoring Structure (from `itemize` to paragraph), Student Development Outcomes (from `itemize` to paragraph), and Expected Research Outcomes (from `enumerate` to paragraph) — reduces visual clutter while preserving all content with bold callouts for scannability

### Reference updates
- **Removed Lookman (2019) citation** per PI direction and replaced BO application examples with three high-impact references from diverse domains:
  - Silver et al. 2016 (*Nature*): AlphaGo hyperparameter tuning
  - Ament et al. 2023 (NeurIPS Workshop): Sustainable concrete formulations via BO
  - Strieth-Kalthoff et al. 2024 (*Science*): Closed-loop discovery of organic laser emitters
- Background BO paragraph now frames broad impact: "BO has driven breakthroughs across domains—from tuning hyperparameters of AlphaGo to optimizing sustainable concrete formulations and discovering state-of-the-art organic laser emitters"

### Budget (`sections/budget.tex`)
- Consolidated to MRG template categories: undergraduate wages, graduate wages, supplies, travel, other
- Folded "Sensors & DAQ" and "Software & computing" into Supplies
- Compressed budget justification to fit 5-page body limit with properly scoped `\small` font size
- **Restructured for full-time summer work**: Undergraduate wages increased to $18,000 ($9,000/yr) to cover part-time (~10 hrs/week) during fall/winter semesters and full-time (~40 hrs/week) during summer terms; other categories adjusted (grad wages $2,500, supplies $2,500, travel $1,500, other $500) to maintain $25,000 total
- Student count updated to 2 (matching budget allocation) throughout proposal, cover page, and expected outcomes

### Timeline
- **Expanded to 6 periods**: Added Y1 Summer and Y2 Summer columns to reflect full-time summer research effort
- Summer-intensive activities: Go/No-Go gate validation, BO implementation, fabrication, and impact testing concentrated during full-time summer terms
- Journal manuscript preparation extends into Y2 Summer

### References (`references.bib`)
- Added `mo2023accelerated` (doi:10.1061/JENMDT.EMENG-7033)
- Added `pajunen2019design`, `ye2023multimaterial`, `khatri2024energy` (Edison-recommended)
- Added `silver2016mastering` (AlphaGo, Nature), `ament2023sustainable` (concrete, arXiv), `striethkalthoff2024delocalized` (dye lasers, Science)
- Removed `lookman2019active` per PI direction
- Fixed `wang2022bayesian` and `lee2023bayesian` with volume/pages/DOI
- Removed `\todo` commands

### Review comment fixes
- Fixed "masters" → "master's" possessive throughout (proposal.tex, budget.tex)
- Expanded "fab." → "fabrication" in timeline table for consistency
- Converted cover page budget from floating `table` to non-floating `center` environment to prevent drift
- Fixed `[h]` → `[ht]` float specifiers to eliminate LaTeX warnings

### Housekeeping
- `Makefile`: added new section files as dependencies
- `.gitignore`: track compiled `proposal.pdf` so the built output is visible in the repo
- `README.md`: updated to reflect new structure
- **`proposal.pdf`**: compiled PDF committed and tracked in git for easy review (10 pages: 2 cover + 5 body + 1 references + 2 biosketches, zero LaTeX warnings)
- **`proposal-diff.pdf`**: latexdiff PDF showing changes per copilot-instructions.md conventions

# Tensegrity MRG Proposal Revision Plan

## Context

- **PI:** Jeffrey R. Hill, Mechanical Engineering (Associate Professor)
- **Co-PI:** Sterling G. Baird, Mechanical Engineering
- **Grant:** BYU Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering Mentored Research Grant (MRG)
- **Budget:** Up to $25,000 over 2 years
- **Deadline:** March 15, 2026
- **Submission:** Tim McLain at mclain@byu.edu

## MRG Guidelines Summary (from MRG_2026.pdf)

- **Length:** Up to 5 pages, plus coversheet, references, and bio sketch
- **Eligibility:** Full-time faculty in Fulton College of Engineering
- **Purpose:** Support strong mentored learning environments for undergraduates
- **Expected outcomes:** Research products (e.g., peer-reviewed publications)
- **Budget restrictions:** MRGs do not cover tuition, equipment, or faculty wages
- **Necessary criteria:** Focus on mentoring undergrads, consistent with scholarship responsibilities, full-time faculty PI, scholarship outcomes
- **Distinguishing criteria:** Quality of mentoring experience, potential impact of work

## Key Insights from Example Grant (Dillon & Hill 2023)

# Tensegrity MRG Proposal Revision Plan

## Context

- **PI:** Jeffrey R. Hill, Mechanical Engineering (Associate Professor)
- **Co-PI:** Sterling G. Baird, Mechanical Engineering
- **Grant:** BYU Ira A. Fulton College of Engineering Mentored Research Grant (MRG)
- **Budget:** Up to $25,000 over 2 years
- **Deadline:** March 15, 2026
- **Submission:** Tim McLain at mclain@byu.edu

## MRG Guidelines Summary (from MRG_2026.pdf)

- **Length:** Up to 5 pages, plus coversheet, references, and bio sketch
- **Eligibility:** Full-time faculty in Fulton College of Engineering
- **Purpose:** Support strong mentored learning environments for undergraduates
- **Expected outcomes:** Research products (e.g., peer-reviewed publications)
- **Budget restrictions:** MRGs do not cover tuition, equipment, or faculty wages
- **Necessary criteria:** Focus on mentoring undergrads, consistent with scholarship responsibilities, full-time faculty PI, scholarship outcomes
- **Distinguishing criteria:** Quality of mentoring experience, potential impact of work

## Key Insights from Example Grant (Dillon & Hill 2023)

The Dillon–Hill Nitinol stent proposal is a strong model. Key patterns to replicate:

1. **Cover page** includes: title, PI/Co-PI, 150-word abstract, student counts, budget table (undergrad wages / grad wages / supplies / travel / other), relationship to external funding

5. **External funding tie-in:** MRG framed as seed funding for a larger grant (NIH R15 in their case)
6. **Outcomes are concrete:** Named conferences (UCUR, BMES, ASME SMASIS), named journals, and a specific external grant proposal
7. **Bio sketches** use NSF/NIH format with personal statement, positions, products, synergistic activities

4. **Key reference:** Mo, Perdikaris & Raney (2023) "Accelerated Design of Architected Materials with Multifidelity Bayesian Optimization" — ASCE J. Eng. Mech. doi:10.1061/JENMDT.EMENG-7033
5. **Multifidelity BO angle:** Use simulations as low-fidelity + experiments as high-fidelity (directly parallels Mo et al.)

### 1. Create Cover Page (new file: `sections/coverpage.tex`)
- [ ] Title
- [ ] PI: Jeffrey R. Hill, Mechanical Engineering
- [ ] Co-PI: Sterling G. Baird, Mechanical Engineering
- [ ] Abstract (≤150 words) — rewrite Project Summary to be concise

Current structure is too long and academic. Reorganize to match the successful Dillon–Hill example:

- [ ] **Research Motivation and Overview** (combine current Project Summary + first part of Background)
- [ ] **Background** (condense current Background — tensegrity + BO + energy absorption into ~1 page)

- [ ] **Mentoring Environment** (adapt current Mentoring Plan, add Dillon-style details: lab group meetings, literature reviews, student presentations, second-year peer mentoring)
- [ ] **Expected Research Outcomes** (concrete: named conferences, named journals, external grant target)
- [ ] **Potential Impact of Work** (condense current Broader Impacts)
- [ ] **References** (keep separate, doesn't count toward 5 pages)
- [ ] **Bio Sketches** (Hill + Baird, doesn't count toward 5 pages)

### 3. Content Updates
- [ ] Replace generic tensegrity description with **multi-material 3D printed tensegrity** (TPU strings + PLA rods)
- [ ] Add Mo et al. (2023) as key reference and frame the multifidelity BO approach around it
